빨래터에서 무릎을 꿇고 방망이질을 했습니다. 빨래보다 이웃 소문이 더 빨: Kneeling at the washing place, you beat the laundry with a paddle. The neighbours' gossip went round faster than the washing.

Late at night you helped print an uncensored pamphlet at the print shop. It mocked a minister and the queen.
견직물 주문이 끊겨 직기가 몇 주째 멈췄습니다. 상인은 공임을 깎자고 합: Orders for silk stopped and the looms have stood idle for weeks. The merchant wants to cut piece rates.

빵 한 덩이 값이 하루 품삯의 절반을 넘었습니다. 수프에 빵을 덜 넣고: A loaf of bread costs more than half a day's wage. You put less bread in the soup and more water.
선술집에서 글을 아는 사람이 신문을 큰 소리로 읽어 주었습니다. 모두 숨: At the tavern, someone who could read read the newspaper aloud. Everyone held their breath to hear the news from the Assembly.
강가의 날염 공장에서 쏟아낸 염료 때문에 로베크 강물이 날마다 다른 색으: The dye pouring out of the print works along its banks turns the Robec a different colour every day. Rouen lives on cotton.

영국 해군의 봉쇄로 배가 들어오지 않습니다. 부두에는 일감을 찾는 사람만: The Royal Navy's blockade keeps the ships away. The quays are crowded with nothing but men looking for work.

영지 관리인이 소작료와 숲 판매 장부를 들고 왔습니다. 올해 수입은 작년: The steward brought the ledgers of rents and timber sales. This year's income is a little down on last year's.
일요일마다 광장에서 국민방위대 훈련을 받습니다. 총을 메고 줄을 맞추는: Every Sunday you drill with the National Guard in the square. Shouldering a musket and keeping in line is harder than it looks.

영국과 평화 조약이 맺어졌습니다. 10년 만의 평화에 사람들이 거리에서: A peace treaty has been signed with Britain. People drank toasts in the streets to the first peace in ten years.
정교 협약으로 성당이 다시 문을 열고 부활절 종이 울렸습니다. 노인들이: Under the Concordat the church reopened and the Easter bells rang. Old people wept as they went in to Mass.

열여덟 살도 안 된 이웃 소년들까지 군대로 끌려갔습니다. 사람들은 그들을: Even neighbour boys not yet eighteen have been taken for the army. People call them the ‘Marie-Louises’.
동맹군 병사 두 명이 집에 묵게 되었습니다. 먹을 것과 땔감을 내줘야 합: Two Allied soldiers have been quartered in your house. You must give them food and firewood.

장날 북새통에 진열대의 물건이 사라졌습니다. 뒤쫓아 갔지만 골목에서 놓쳤: In the market-day crush, goods vanished from your stall. You gave chase but lost the thief in the alleys.
구청에서 영업세(파탕트) 고지서가 왔습니다. 가게 크기와 창문 수에 따라: A demand for the trading licence tax, the patente, came from the town hall. It is assessed on the size of the shop and the number of windows, and you seriously thought of boarding up a window.
건너편 새 가게: A new shop across the street
길 건너에 같은 물건을 파는 가게가 문을 열었습니다. 값을 한 수 내려: A shop selling the same goods opened across the street. It marked its prices a sou lower, and a few of your regulars crossed over.
이십 년 단골인 노부인이 손녀를 데리고 와서 “이 집 물건이 제일이란다”: An old lady who has been a customer for twenty years brought her granddaughter and told her, “This shop has the best of everything.”
큰마음 먹고 가게 앞을 넓은 유리 진열창으로 바꾸었습니다. 지나가던 사람: You took the plunge and gave the shop front a wide glass window. Passers-by stop and look in.
이웃이 밤사이 밭 경계석을 한 뼘 옮겨 놓았습니다. 마을 원로들 앞에서: Overnight a neighbour moved the boundary stone of your field a hand's breadth. Voices were raised before the village elders, but nothing was settled.
돼지나 먹는 것이라던 감자를 밭 한 귀퉁이에 처음 심어 보았습니다. 흉년: For the first time you planted potatoes, which people say are only fit for pigs, in a corner of the field. To keep from starving in a bad year you have to try anything.
이웃 셋과 품을 모아 마당에 우물을 팠습니다. 열두 자를 파 내려가자 찬: You pooled labour with three neighbours and dug a well in the yard. Twelve feet down, cold water welled up.
공증인 앞에서 얼마 안 되는 밭을 자식들 몫으로 나누었습니다. 똑같이 나: Before the notary you divided your few fields among your children. Under the new law of equal shares, each one's portion came out the size of a palm.
예전 같지 않은 허리: A back that isn't what it was
아들 또래 일꾼들과 나란히 낫질을 했는데, 해가 기울기도 전에 허리가 펴: You swung the scythe beside labourers your son's age, but before the sun was low you could not straighten your back.
봄 씨앗값을 마을 부농에게 빌렸습니다. 가을에 곡식으로 갚되, 한 말에: You borrowed the money for spring seed from the village's rich farmer. You will repay in grain in the autumn, half a measure more for every measure.
그레브 광장의 새벽: Dawn at the Place de Grève
새벽 다섯 시, 일감을 찾는 사내들 틈에 서서 십장의 손짓을 기다렸습니다: At five in the morning you stood among the men looking for work and waited for the foreman's nod. Today you were lucky and picked to haul stone.
강이 얼고 공사가 멈추자 일감이 뚝 끊겼습니다. 외투를 전당포에 맡기고: When the river froze and building stopped, the work dried up at once. You pawned your coat and bought bread.
짐을 내리다 손가락이 돌 사이에 끼었습니다. 일주일 동안 품삯 없이 손을: Unloading, you caught a finger between two stones. For a week you sat with your hand bound up and no wages.
일주일 일한 품삯을 받으러 갔더니 주인이 공사가 끝나지 않았다며 절반만: When you went for a week's wages, the master said the job wasn't finished and paid only half. There is nowhere to complain.
우르크 운하와 새 시장 공사장에 일손이 모자라 품삯이 올랐습니다. 몇 달: The Ourcq canal and the new market halls were short of hands, so wages rose. For a few months you lived with the smell of meat on the table.
주인집 은수저 한 벌이 없어지자 모두의 눈이 당신에게 쏠렸습니다. 사흘: When a set of the household's silver spoons went missing, every eye turned to you. Three days later they turned up behind the dresser, but no one apologised.
한 달에 한 번 얻는 일요일 오후, 같은 고향 출신 하녀들과 성곽 밖 선: On your one Sunday afternoon a month, you danced with maids from your home region at a tavern beyond the walls.
모은 품삯을 고향 가는 짐마차꾼 편에 부쳤습니다. 글을 아는 동료가 대신: You sent your savings home with a carter going that way. A workmate who could write wrote the letter for you.
주인 나리가 재혼해 새 마님이 들어왔습니다. 첫날부터 은그릇 닦는 법이: The master remarried and a new mistress came into the house. From the first day she said you polished the silver wrong and made you start again.
열세 살 아이를 도제로 받았습니다. 부모가 계약서에 서명 대신 십자를 그: You took a thirteen-year-old as an apprentice. The parents drew a cross on the indenture instead of signing, and that night the child cried in the attic.
Journeymen on their Tour de France stopped at the workshop with their canes and ribbons. They have greetings and songs only they know.
새 작업장으로 옮기려면 노동자 수첩(리브레)에 옛 주인의 서명을 받아야: To move to a new workshop you need your old master's signature in your livret. He put off signing, saying you still owed him money.
좋은 집안의 혼례를 앞두고 큰 주문이 들어왔습니다. 석 달 동안 밤늦게까: A big order came in ahead of a wedding in a good family. For three months you kept the lamp burning late, but your purse grew fat.
먼지와 기름 연기 속에서 이십 년을 일했더니 아침마다 기침이 멎지 않습니: After twenty years of work in dust and oil smoke, the cough will not stop in the mornings.
파리의 유행이 바뀌어 비단 주문이 끊겼습니다. 언덕 위 크루아루스의 직기: Paris fashions changed and silk orders dried up. One by one, the looms up on the Croix-Rousse fell silent.
등불을 들고 밤거리를 돌았습니다. 술 취한 직인 둘을 떼어 놓고, 길 잃: You walked the streets at night with a lantern. You pulled apart two drunken journeymen and took a lost child home.
이웃이 이웃을 고발하는 쪽지가 매주 책상에 쌓입니다. 대부분은 빚이나 질: Every week notes in which neighbour denounces neighbour pile up on the desk. Most come from debts or jealousy.
자정이 넘어 문을 두드리는 소리에 가방을 챙겨 나섰습니다. 진흙길을 한: At a knock on the door after midnight you took your bag and set out. After an hour's walk down a muddy road you arrived before dawn.
아기가 거꾸로 들어선 출산이었습니다. 아이는 살렸지만 어머니는 사흘 뒤: The baby was breech. You saved the child, but the mother died of fever three days later.
마을 아이들에게 우두를 접종했습니다. 소의 고름을 넣는다는 말에 겁먹은: You vaccinated the village children against smallpox. When frightened parents heard it meant putting in pus from a cow, you went from house to house to persuade them.
글을 깨친 아이: A child who learned to read
가을 내내 더듬거리던 대장장이 아들이 처음으로 한 쪽을 막힘없이 읽었습니: The blacksmith's son, who had stumbled all autumn, read a whole page without a stop for the first time. You were happier than he was.
부활절을 앞두고 줄지은 고해를 들었습니다. 이웃의 비밀을 너무 많이 알게: Before Easter you heard a long line of confessions. Knowing too many of your neighbours' secrets is a burden too.
열몇 살 아이가 처음으로 정면에서 말대꾸를 했습니다. 문을 쾅 닫고 나간: Your child, now in their teens, answered you back to your face for the first time. After the door slammed, supper was quiet.
아이를 남의 작업장에 도제로 보냈습니다. 보따리 하나 들고 돌아보지 않으: You sent your child to apprentice in someone else's workshop. You watched for a long time as they walked off with a single bundle, trying not to look back.
딸의 혼수 궤짝에 홑이불과 수건을 한 장씩 모아 넣고 있습니다. 머리글자: One sheet and one towel at a time, you are filling your daughter's bridal chest. She embroidered the initials herself.
첫 손주가 태어났습니다. 세례식에서 대부모가 아기를 안는 동안, 당신은: Your first grandchild was born. While the godparents held the baby at the christening, you secretly wiped your eyes in the back row.
나이 드신 부모님이 계단을 오르내리기 힘들어하셔서 침대를 아래층 부엌 옆: Your elderly parents were finding the stairs hard, so you moved their bed downstairs beside the kitchen.
하루 일을 마치고 배우자와 난롯가에 앉아 오랜만에 젊을 적 이야기를 했습: After the day's work you sat by the fire with your spouse and talked about your young days for the first time in a long while. You both laughed more than you did back then.
선술집 외상값 때문에 배우자와 크게 다투었습니다. 사흘 동안 서로 필요한: You had a bad quarrel with your spouse over a tavern slate. For three days you said only what had to be said.
어릴 적부터 알던 친구의 장례 행렬을 따라 묘지까지 걸었습니다. 같은 해: You followed the funeral procession of a friend you had known since childhood all the way to the cemetery. One by one, those born in your year are fewer.
어금니가 아파 장터 이 뽑는 사람에게 갔습니다. 북 치는 소리에 비명이: A molar ached, so you went to the tooth-puller at the fair. The drumming drowned out your scream, and now you chew on one side only.
글씨가 흐려 보여 행상에게서 돋보기안경을 샀습니다. 코에 걸자 세상이 다: The writing had blurred, so you bought reading spectacles from a pedlar. When you put them on your nose, the world was sharp again.
우물물에 비친 얼굴을 보다가 귀밑의 흰머리를 발견했습니다. 어머니가 꼭: Looking at your face in the well water, you noticed grey hair at your temples. Your mother was just this age when hers turned, you think.
침대 밑 양말 속에 모은 돈을 세어 보니 생각보다 많았습니다. 처음으로: Counting the money saved in a stocking under the bed, you found more than you expected. For the first time you thought you would not go hungry in old age.
생탄 도레의 대파르동에 걸어서 다녀왔습니다. 수만 명이 촛불을 들고 밤새: You walked to the Grand Pardon of Sainte-Anne-d'Auray. Tens of thousands held candles and sang all night in Breton.
폭풍이 지나간 아침, 해안에 배 한 척이 부서져 있었습니다. 마을 사람들: On the morning after the storm a ship lay broken on the shore. The villagers scrambled to carry off casks and planks.
추수가 끝나자 마을 사내들과 함께 파리로 겨울 돈벌이를 떠났습니다. 물을: When the harvest was in, you left for Paris with the village men to earn money over the winter. You will carry water and sell charcoal, and come home in spring.
The great cheese made on the summer pastures fetched a good price at market.
새순이 돋은 포도밭에 늦서리가 내렸습니다. 밤새 밭고랑에 짚불을 피웠지만: A late frost fell on the vines just as the buds broke. You burned straw in the rows all night, but half were blackened.
올해 포도주는 빛깔이 깊고 맛이 부드럽습니다. 본의 중개상이 술통을 두드: This year's wine is deep in colour and smooth. The broker from Beaune tapped the casks and named a generous price.
샤르트롱 부두에서 포도주 통을 굴려 배에 싣는 소리가 종일 그치지 않습니: On the Chartrons quay the rumble of wine casks being rolled aboard ships never stops all day. You hear English and Dutch as often as French.
대륙 봉쇄로 영국 배가 끊기자 항구에 돛대가 사라졌습니다. 술통이 창고에: When the Continental Blockade cut off the English ships, the masts vanished from the harbour. The casks gather dust in the warehouses.
센강 계곡의 면직 공장에서 새벽 종이 울리면 아이들까지 줄지어 공장 문으: When the dawn bell rings at the cotton mills of the Seine valley, even children file in through the factory gates.
눈 녹은 물로 루아르강이 둑을 넘었습니다. 강가 집들의 아래층이 무릎까지: Swollen with snowmelt, the Loire burst its banks. The ground floors of the riverside houses stood knee-deep in water.
직기 높이에 맞춰 천장이 높은 크루아루스의 새 건물들로 직조공들이 옮겨: Weavers are moving into the new buildings on the Croix-Rousse, built with ceilings high enough for the looms. On rainy days the silk is carried through the traboules, the covered passages.
타유세 징수원이 마을 명부를 들고 왔습니다. 지붕을 새로 이은 집일수록: The taille collector came with the village roll. Rumour says a new roof means a higher tax, so everyone leaves their old roofs as they are.
문과 창문의 세금: A tax on doors and windows
문과 창문 수에 매기는 세금 고지서가 왔습니다. 집 뒤 창 하나를 벽돌로: The bill came for the tax on the number of doors and windows. More and more houses are bricking up a window at the back.
분기 집세를 내는 날입니다. 집주인이 내년부터 집세를 올리겠다고 했습니다: It is quarter day, when the rent is due. The landlord said he would raise the rent from next year. You worked out whether to move up to an attic room.
무더위에 우물물이 상해 온 동네에 설사병이 돌았습니다. 당신도 열흘을 앓: In the heat the well water went bad and the flux spread through the whole neighbourhood. You were ill for ten days, and two children next door died.
밤사이 닭장의 암탉 세 마리가 사라졌습니다. 여우인지 떠돌이인지, 아침: Three hens vanished from the coop overnight. Fox or vagrant, in the morning there were only feathers scattered across the field.
마른 짚단에 불이 붙어 헛간 한쪽이 탔습니다. 온 마을이 양동이를 들고: Dry straw caught fire and one end of the barn burned. The whole village came running with buckets and at least kept it from spreading to the house.
빨래터 말다툼: A quarrel at the washing place
빨래터 자리를 두고 이웃 여자와 말다툼이 붙었습니다. 그 집 딸 혼삿말까: You fell out with a neighbour woman over a place at the washing place. You ended up bringing her daughter's marriage prospects into it, and avoided her eyes for some time after.
시어머니는 아직도 수프에 소금을 얼마나 넣는지 지켜봅니다. 부엌의 주인은: Your mother-in-law still watches how much salt you put in the soup. The kitchen is still hers.
지난가을 곡식이 바닥났는데 새 곡식은 아직 멀었습니다. 밤과 메밀죽으로: Last autumn's grain has run out and the new harvest is still far off. For a month you got by on chestnuts and buckwheat porridge.
물려받은 땅 한 뙈기를 두고 사촌과 송사가 붙었습니다. 공증인과 변호사에: You went to law with a cousin over a scrap of inherited land. What you paid the notary and the lawyer came to as much as the land is worth.
수호성인 축일 장이 섰습니다. 약장수와 줄타기꾼, 이 뽑는 사람이 한꺼번: The fair for the patron saint's day was held. Quack doctors, rope-dancers and tooth-pullers took over the square all at once.
관청에 낼 청원서를 쓰려고 장터의 대서인에게 몇 수를 냈습니다. 그가 읽: You paid a few sous to the letter-writer at the market to write a petition to the authorities. The sentences he read back did not sound like anything you had said.
저녁마다 이웃들이 모여 당신이 신문을 소리 내어 읽는 것을 듣습니다. 글: Every evening the neighbours gather to hear you read the newspaper aloud. Knowing how to read draws people like this.
11월 11일 생마르탱 날, 소작 계약과 일꾼 고용이 한꺼번에 갱신됩니다: On 11 November, Saint Martin's Day, leases and farmhands' hiring are all renewed at once. People with sacks of rent on their backs lined up outside the landowner's house.
만성절에 먼저 간 가족들의 무덤을 찾아 국화를 놓았습니다. 묘지는 해마다: On All Saints' Day you visited the graves of family gone before and laid chrysanthemums. Every year there are more names you know in the cemetery.
부활절 영성체를 하지 않으면 신부가 명단을 적어 둡니다. 일 년에 한 번: The priest writes down the names of those who do not take Easter communion. Once a year, nearly everyone in the village stands in line at the confessional.
한여름 일꾼 장에서 머리에 밀 이삭을 꽂고 서 있었습니다. 일꾼이라는 표: At the midsummer hiring fair you stood with an ear of wheat in your hat, the sign of a farmhand for hire. A rich farmer looked at your palms and named a wage.
관청은 열흘째 날(데카디)에 쉬라고 하지만, 마을 사람들은 여전히 일요일: The authorities say to rest on the tenth day, the décadi, but the villagers still down tools on Sunday. The priest who comes in secret says Mass in a barn.
사순절 전 마지막 밤, 가면을 쓰고 광장에서 춤을 추었습니다. 짚으로 만: On the last night before Lent you danced in the square in a mask. You saw the winter out by burning the straw figure of Carnival.
하루 종일 진흙길을 행군했습니다. 배낭 무게에 어깨가 끊어질 것 같습니다: You marched down muddy roads all day. The weight of your pack feels as if it will tear your shoulders off. In the evening you dropped and slept in a roadside field.
보급 마차가 오지 않아 사흘 동안 딱딱한 비스킷 반쪽으로 버텼습니다. 동: The supply wagons did not come, and for three days you lived on half a hard biscuit. Your comrades are eyeing the farms nearby.
고향에서 편지가 왔습니다. 글을 아는 동료가 읽어 주었습니다. 가족은 모: A letter came from home. A comrade who could read read it to you. The family are all safe.
모닥불 가에서 동료들과 고향 노래를 불렀습니다. 노르망디, 프로방스, 브: Around the fire you sang songs from home with your comrades. Norman, Provençal and Breton accents all mixed together.
야영지에 이가 들끓고 열병이 돌았습니다. 며칠 동안 야전 병원에 누워 있: The camp swarmed with lice and fever went round. You lay in the field hospital for some days.
하사의 구령에 맞춰 장전과 사격을 수십 번 반복했습니다. 손이 저절로 움: To the corporal's commands you loaded and fired dozens of times, until your hands moved on their own.
처음 보는 강과 마을을 지났습니다. 사람들 말을 한마디도 알아들을 수 없: You passed rivers and villages you had never seen. You cannot understand a word people say.
Your mother wrapped you in swaddling clothes, held you close and sang you a quiet lullaby.
The family took you to the parish church to be baptised.
처음으로 혼자 몇 걸음을 걸었습니다. 곁에서 돌보던 어른이 반가워했습니다: You walked a few steps on your own for the first time. The grown-up watching over you was delighted.
As money grew tight, the family began to save on firewood for heating.
While your mother worked, a neighbour woman looked after you.
You spent a long time watching the carriages go by outside the window.
Back from the market, your mother handed you a small piece of fruit.
For the first time you played with the other children in the lane outside the house.
Your father made you a little toy from a piece of wood.
You got your shoes covered in mud playing in the lane and were scolded at home.
You quarrelled with the neighbours' child over a toy, but soon made up.
You went to the market with your mother and watched the stallholders haggle.
Your grandmother told you an old folk tale she had heard as a child.
You were scolded for handling one of your father's tools.
이웃집 아이가 글자를 읽는 모습을 보고 자신도 배워 보고 싶다고 생각했습: Seeing the neighbours' child read, you wished you could learn too.
As the cold deepened, the family spent their time gathered close to the fire.
You watched a religious procession through the neighbourhood and stared at the decorations for a long time.
Sent to the baker's, you struggled to count the change.
A friend who goes to the parish school showed off the letters they had learned.
Helping your mother, you ran an errand by yourself for the first time.
You spent a long time in a craftsman's workshop watching him shape wood.
Buying something at the market, you noticed the change was wrong.
Your father gave you the job of cleaning the workshop.
You wandered along the Seine with a friend and came home late.
가족이 장래에 어떤 일을 하고 싶은지 물었습니다. 당신은 한참을 고민했습: Your family asked what work you would like to do one day. You thought about it for a long time.
A craftsman in the neighbourhood asked you to help with a simple job.
As things got harder at home, the family decided to spend less.
You fiddled for ages trying to fix a wooden top that would not spin properly.
You helped sort scraps of leather in your father's workshop.
Looking at your father's ledger, you learned a little about reading numbers.

집 앞의 길과 사람들의 말소리가 조금씩 익숙해집니다. 낯선 일이 생겼을: The road outside the house and the sound of people's voices are growing familiar. When something strange happens, how will little you react? Choices at this age are made within the family's care.
가까운 어른의 손을 잡는다: Hold the hand of a grown-up close to you
Reassured by a familiar hand, you looked around.
주변을 살피며 말을 따라 해 본다: Look around and try repeating words
You began, little by little, to link the words you heard with the things in front of you.
You spent the day resting and playing at home.
학교에 보내 달라고 부탁할까?: Ask to be sent to school?
이웃집 아이가 교구의 자선학교에 다니기 시작했습니다.\n당신도 글을 배우:
The neighbours' child has started going to the parish charity school.
You want to learn to read too, but your father says he needs someone to run errands in the workshop.
Your mother has said she will hear what you have to ask.
부모에게 학교에 보내 달라고 부탁한다: Ask your parents to send you to school
입학 허락 / 거절 / 조건부 허락: Allowed to go / refused / allowed on conditions
입학을 허락받았습니다: You were allowed to go to school
어머니가 아버지를 설득했습니다. 작업장 일손을 나누기로 하고, 당신은 교: Your mother talked your father round. The work of the workshop will be shared out, and you begin learning to read and reckon at the parish charity school. Books and school things cost a little.
이번에는 허락받지 못했습니다: This time you were not allowed
아버지는 지금은 일손을 줄일 수 없다며 고개를 저었습니다. 학교에 가려던: Your father shook his head: he cannot spare a pair of hands just now. The plan to go to school was put off, but the wish to learn remained. There is still the chance to learn from family or neighbours later.
가업을 돕는 조건으로 허락받았습니다: Allowed, on condition you help in the family trade
부모는 작업장 심부름을 계속한다면 학교에 다녀도 좋다고 했습니다. 배움과: Your parents said you may go to school if you keep running errands for the workshop. Dividing your time between lessons and work makes study slow, but you learn to read and reckon and gain experience of the family trade as well.
이웃에게 글자를 배운다: Learn your letters from a neighbour
비정규 교육 시작 / 부탁 거절: Informal lessons begin / the request is refused
이웃과 작은 배움이 시작됐습니다: Small lessons with a neighbour began
이웃은 일이 끝난 뒤 잠시 시간을 내 주기로 했습니다. 당신은 종이 조각: The neighbour agreed to give you a little time after work. You copy letters on scraps of paper and learn to read. Time spent learning outside school and practising on your own adds up.
이웃이 시간을 내기 어렵다고 했습니다: The neighbour said they could not find the time
이웃도 생업 때문에 가르칠 여유가 없다며 미안해했습니다. 이번 부탁으로: The neighbour apologised: work leaves no time to teach. This request did not lead to lessons. You hold on to your wish to learn and wait for the next chance.
지금은 가업을 돕는다: Help in the family trade for now
가업 경험 증가 / 교육 기회 감소: More experience of the trade / fewer chances to study
작업장에서 배우는 날들이 시작됐습니다: Days of learning in the workshop began
당신은 아버지의 작업장에서 심부름을 맡기로 했습니다. 가족의 수입을 보태: You agreed to run errands in your father's workshop. You add to the family's income and learn the tools and the order of the work. While you help there is less time to learn to read, but later you can make time for learning again.
이웃 마을에서 천연두가 돌고 있습니다. 의사는 천연두 환자의 고름을 조금: Smallpox is going round the next village. The doctor recommends ‘inoculation’: putting in a little matter from a smallpox patient to bring on a mild case. Usually it passes lightly, but now and then, they say, a child falls badly ill.
평생 면역 / 며칠 앓음 / 크게 앓음: Lifelong protection / ill for a few days / badly ill
가볍게 앓고 지나갔습니다: A mild case, and it passed
The fever rose for a few days and then broke. You need not fear smallpox any more.
열흘 가까이 앓았습니다: You were ill for nearly ten days
You were ill longer than expected and the family fretted, but in the end you recovered.
크게 앓고 흉터가 남았습니다: You were badly ill and left with scars
A high fever kept you in bed for a long time. Faint scars remain on your face.
하느님의 뜻에 맡기고 기다린다: Leave it to God's will and wait
You were not inoculated. Fortunately this outbreak passed the village by.
유행이 지나갈 때까지 아이를 친척 집에 보낸다: Send the child to relatives until the outbreak passes
You stayed with relatives for a while. It was a strange place, but you came home safe.
옆 골목에서 천연두가 돌고 있습니다. 시립 병원의 의사는 천연두 환자의: Smallpox is going round the next street. The doctor at the city hospital recommends ‘inoculation’: putting in a little matter from a smallpox patient to bring on a mild case. Usually it passes lightly, but now and then, they say, a child falls badly ill.
{고향}의 아랫동네에서 천연두가 돌고 있습니다. 의사는 천연두 환자의 고: Smallpox is going round the lower town of {고향}. The doctor recommends ‘inoculation’: putting in a little matter from a smallpox patient to bring on a mild case. Usually it passes lightly, but now and then, they say, a child falls badly ill.
영국에서 들어온 ‘우두’ 접종이 마을에서도 시행된다고 합니다. 소의 고름: They say the ‘cowpox’ vaccination brought over from England is being given in the village too. Some grown-ups are uneasy because it uses matter from cows.
A small sore came up on your arm and healed. Your worry about smallpox is eased.
소문이 미덥지 않아 미룬다: The rumours sound doubtful; put it off
Your parents decided to wait and see a little longer.
영국에서 들어온 ‘우두’ 접종을 시청에서 무료로 놓아 준다고 합니다. 소: They say the town hall is giving the ‘cowpox’ vaccination brought over from England free of charge. Some neighbours are uneasy because it uses matter from cows.
영국에서 들어온 ‘우두’ 접종을 {고향} 시립 병원에서 놓아 준다고 합니: They say the town hospital in {고향} is giving the ‘cowpox’ vaccination brought over from England. Some neighbours are uneasy because it uses matter from cows.
본당 신부가 올해 첫영성체를 받을 아이들을 모읍니다. 몇 달 동안 교리: The parish priest is gathering the children who will make their First Communion this year. You must learn the catechism by heart over several months, and new clothes must be found.
교리 문답을 외워 신부의 칭찬을 받았습니다. 흰 옷을 입고 첫영성체를 받: You learned the catechism by heart and the priest praised you. You made your First Communion dressed in white.
일을 도우며 틈틈이 다닌다: Go when you can, between chores
Your studies were slow, but you made your First Communion without mishap.
내년으로 미룬다: Put it off until next year
You were not ready this year. The neighbours whispered.
농사일이 한가한 겨울 몇 달 동안 마을 학교가 열립니다. 교사는 성당지기: In the winter months, when there is little farm work, the village school opens. The teacher is also the sexton, and the fees are a few sous a month.
겨울 학교에 보내 달라고 조른다: Beg to be sent to the winter school
입학 / 형편상 거절: You go / turned down for lack of money
겨울 동안 학교에 다녔습니다: You went to school over the winter
난롯가에 둘러앉아 글자와 셈을 배웠습니다. 봄이 되면 다시 들일을 돕습니: Sitting round the stove, you learned your letters and sums. In spring you will help in the fields again.
수업료를 낼 형편이 안 됩니다: The family cannot afford the fees
Your father was already worried about this winter's firewood. School was put off until another time.
집에서 가축을 돌본다: Look after the animals at home
You spent the winter tending the animals and helping with the housework.
가문의 아이를 어떻게 가르칠까: How to educate a child of the family
가문의 체면에 맞는 교육을 정할 때입니다. 집에 가정교사를 들일 수도,: It is time to choose an education worthy of the family name. You could bring a tutor into the house, send the child to boarding school, or have them prepare to be a soldier.
집에 가정교사를 들인다: Bring a tutor into the house
At home you learn Latin and French composition, dancing and manners.
수도회 기숙 학교에 보낸다: Send them to a boarding school run by a religious order
You learn the classics and the faith under strict discipline. You miss home.
You began learning mathematics, riding and fencing.
부모는 당신을 라틴어를 가르치는 학교에 보낼지, 일찍 장부 쓰는 법을 가: Your parents are weighing whether to send you to a school that teaches Latin or teach you to keep the books early. School is the door to getting on in the world, but it costs money.
학교에서 고전 교육을 받는다: Get a classical education at school
You won a prize for Latin composition and became the pride of the family.
Your marks are middling, but you have made plenty of friends.
가게에서 장부와 셈을 배운다: Learn the books and figures in the shop
Behind the counter you learn to serve customers and keep the books.
이웃의 큰 농가에서 여름 내내 양을 칠 아이를 구합니다. 먹여 주고 가을: A big farm nearby is looking for a child to mind sheep all summer. Board is provided, and wages paid in the autumn.
여름 동안 양치기로 간다: Go as a shepherd for the summer
들판에서 혼자 양 떼를 지키며 여름을 보냈습니다. 가을에 받은 품삯을 어: You spent the summer alone in the fields, watching the flock. You gave the wages you earned in the autumn to your mother.
You spent the summer helping with the housework.
파리로 굴뚝 청소하러 갈까?: Go to Paris to sweep chimneys?
겨울마다 오베르뉴의 아이들이 파리로 내려가 굴뚝을 청소하고 봄에 돌아옵니: Every winter, children from the Auvergne go down to Paris to sweep chimneys and come back in spring. One of the village men is looking for children to take this year.
돈을 벌어 옴 / 병을 얻음: Come back with money / come back ill
봄에 돈을 벌어 돌아왔습니다: You came back in spring with money
좁은 굴뚝을 오르내리며 겨울을 났습니다. 그을음투성이였지만 모은 돈을 들: You got through the winter climbing up and down narrow chimneys. You were black with soot, but you came home with your savings.
기침병을 얻어 돌아왔습니다: You came back with a cough
그을음과 추위에 기침이 떨어지지 않았습니다. 돈은 조금밖에 못 모았습니다: With the soot and the cold, the cough would not leave you. You saved only a little.
This winter you stayed with your family.
새로 들어선 방적 공장이 아이들을 고용합니다. 하루 열두 시간 넘게 일하: The new spinning mill is hiring children. The work is more than twelve hours a day, but money comes into the house regularly.
Your job is to piece the broken threads. Your hands have grown quick, but you are always tired.
부모가 조금 더 버텨 보기로 한다: Your parents decide to hold out a little longer
Money is tight at home, but for now you stayed at home.
먼저 도시로 간 사촌이 부잣집 하녀 자리를 알아봐 주겠다고 합니다. 숙식: A cousin who went to town first offers to find you a place as a maid in a rich house. Bed and board are provided and you could save a dowry, but people say it all depends on the master you get.
하녀로 들어간다: Go into service as a maid
좋은 주인 / 고된 집: A good master / a hard house
마님은 엄격하지만 공정했습니다. 품삯을 차곡차곡 모으고 글자도 조금 배웠: The mistress was strict but fair. You put your wages by and even learned a few letters.
You worked from dawn to night and were often scolded. Still, you were paid.
고향에서 실을 자아 판다: Spin yarn at home and sell it
You spin yarn at home and sell it to a merchant.
You decided to stay with your family.
같은 골목 아주머니가 생제르맹 포부르의 부잣집 하녀 자리를 알아봐 주겠다: A woman from your lane offers to find you a place as a maid in a rich house in the Faubourg Saint-Germain. Bed and board are provided and you could save a dowry, but people say it all depends on the master you get.
{고향}의 상인 집안에서 하녀를 구한다고 사촌이 알려 왔습니다. 숙식이: A cousin writes that a merchant family in {고향} is looking for a maid. Bed and board are provided and you could save a dowry, but people say it all depends on the master you get.
먼저 {도시}(으)로 간 사촌이 부잣집 하녀 자리를 알아봐 주겠다고 합니: A cousin who went to {도시} first offers to find you a place as a maid in a rich house. Bed and board are provided and you could save a dowry, but people say it all depends on the master you get.
동업 직인 조합의 선배들이 프랑스를 한 바퀴 돌며 여러 도시의 작업장에서: The older members of the compagnonnage urge you to go round France, working in the workshops of different towns. It takes several years, but your skill is sure to grow.
솜씨 좋은 직인이 되어 돌아왔습니다: You came back a skilled journeyman
리옹, 마르세유, 보르도의 작업장을 거쳤습니다. 조합의 별명도 얻었습니다: You worked in the workshops of Lyon, Marseille and Bordeaux, and earned your compagnonnage nickname.
몇 달 만에 돌아왔습니다: You came back after a few months
조합 사이의 싸움에 휘말려 일찍 돌아왔습니다. 그래도 배운 것은 있습니다: You were caught up in a fight between rival compagnonnages and came back early. Still, you learned something.
You work steadily in the workshop you know.
본당 신부가 당신의 총명함을 눈여겨보고 신학교를 권합니다. 성직자가 되면: The parish priest has noticed how bright you are and suggests the seminary. As a priest you could study, but you could never marry.
You began studying Latin and theology. In a few years you will be ordained.
The priest was disappointed but respected your wishes.
혼인을 하려면 지참금이 필요하다는 이야기가 오갑니다. 부모의 형편은 넉넉: There is talk that you will need a dowry to marry. Your parents are not well off.
몇 해 일해 스스로 모은다: Work a few years and save it yourself
You decided to put off marriage and work to save a dowry.
부모가 땅 한 뙈기를 떼어 준다: Your parents set aside a scrap of land
Your parents promised a small field as your dowry. Your brothers and sisters are a little hurt.
지참금 없이 맞아 줄 사람을 찾는다: Look for someone who will take you without a dowry
You decided to trust in love.
지참금 없이 좋은 집안에 시집가기는 어렵습니다. 집안에서는 수녀원에 보내: Without a dowry it is hard to marry into a good family. At home there is even talk that a convent would cost less than a dowry.
상대 집안이 움직이려면 아버지가 지참금 2만 리브르쯤은 약속해야 한다고: For the other family to take any interest, they say, your father would have to promise a dowry of some twenty thousand livres. Over dinner there is talk of how much that would cut your siblings' shares.
하녀나 재봉 일로 몇 해를 모아야 혼수 궤짝을 채울 수 있습니다. 부모님: It will take some years of work as a maid or seamstress to fill your bridal chest. Your parents, living in rented rooms, have almost nothing to give.
아버지가 줄 수 있는 것은 침대 하나와 홑이불 몇 장, 운이 좋으면 암소: All your father can give is a bed, a few sheets and, with luck, a cow. Without a dowry there are few good matches.
겨울밤 이웃집 외양간에 모여 실을 잣고 이야기를 나누는 마실에서, 자꾸: At the winter veillée, where neighbours gather in a byre to spin and talk, there is someone whose eyes keep meeting yours.
춤 축제에서 마음을 고백한다: Declare your feelings at the village dance
두 집안이 합의하고 성당에서 혼인했습니다. 마을 사람들이 사흘 동안 잔치: The two families agreed and you were married in church. The village feasted for three days.
Their parents wanted a better-off match. Your heart ached for a while.
You said nothing. The winter passed.
집안이 정한 혼처: A match arranged by the family
양가 공증인이 혼인 계약서를 준비하고 있습니다. 상대는 집안끼리 잘 맞는: The notaries of both families are drawing up the marriage contract. The other party is well suited as families go, but you have met only a few times.
혼인 계약에 서명하고 혼례를 올렸습니다. 두 집안의 재산이 하나로 묶였습: You signed the marriage contract and the wedding took place. The two families' fortunes were bound into one.
마음에 둔 사람을 고집한다: Insist on the one you love
결국 허락을 받았습니다: In the end you got their consent
Your parents sighed but gave their consent. The dowry was smaller.
부모와 사이가 멀어졌습니다: You grew apart from your parents
The marriage was put off, and things grew cold with your family.
혼인을 미루고 공부·일에 전념한다: Put off marriage and devote yourself to study and work
You politely put off talk of a match.
“모든 프랑스인은 군대에 복무할 의무가 있다.” 미혼 청년부터 차례로 징: “Every Frenchman is bound to serve in the army.” Unmarried young men are called up first. One by one, the village's young men are leaving.
국경으로 출정 / 훈련 중 부상: March to the frontier / injured in training
대대에 배속되었습니다: You were posted to a battalion
You were issued a hat with a tricolour cockade and a musket and posted to a volunteer battalion. A few days later you begin the march to the frontier behind the drums.
훈련 중 다쳐 돌려보내졌습니다: Injured in training and sent home
출정 전 훈련에서 다리를 크게 다쳐 군의관이 복무 부적합 판정을 내렸습니: You badly hurt your leg in training before setting out, and the army surgeon declared you unfit for service. It still aches when rain is coming.
You stayed at home and took on carting army supplies. You do not go to the front.
숲에 숨는다(징집 기피): Hide in the woods (dodge the draft)
You lay hidden for months. The neighbours pretended not to know.
헌병에게 붙잡혔습니다: You were caught by the gendarmes
벌금을 물고 헌병에게 이끌려 가장 가까운 대대로 보내졌습니다. 이제 국경: You were fined and marched by the gendarmes to the nearest battalion. Now you must go to the frontier.
“모든 프랑스인은 군대에 복무할 의무가 있다.” 미혼 청년부터 차례로 징: “Every Frenchman is bound to serve in the army.” Unmarried young men are called up first. The lists are posted outside the section office, and one by one the young men of your street are leaving.

“Every Frenchman is bound to serve in the army.” Unmarried young men are called up first. The lists are posted outside the town hall of {고향}, and one by one the young journeymen of the workshops are leaving.
스무 살이 된 청년들이 면사무소에 모여 번호를 뽑습니다. 나쁜 번호를 뽑: The young men who have turned twenty gather at the town hall to draw numbers. Draw a bad number and you must serve several years in the army. With money you can buy a substitute.
좋은 번호 / 나쁜 번호: A good number / a bad number
You will not have to go into the army. The family lit a candle in church.
You put on the uniform and leave for your regiment.
You paid a large sum for another young man to enlist in your place.
You joined the army of your own accord. You march with your comrades.
저녁마다 구역 회의와 클럽에서 신문을 읽고 연설을 합니다. 이웃들이 당신: Every evening in the section assemblies and clubs people read the newspapers aloud and make speeches. The neighbours want you to come too.
회의에 나가 발언한다: Go to the assembly and speak
For the first time you spoke before an audience. Your name became a little known.
신문만 사서 읽는다: Just buy the newspapers and read them
You read the newspapers quietly at home and keep an eye on how the world is going.
You decided to avoid talk of politics. These days every word must be guarded.
많은 귀족 가문이 국경 너머 코블렌츠로 떠났습니다. 남으면 의심을 받고,: Many noble families have left for Koblenz, across the border. Stay and you will be suspected; leave and your property may be confiscated.
밤에 짐을 꾸려 국경을 넘었습니다. 남겨 둔 땅과 집은 국가에 몰수되었습: You packed at night and crossed the border. The land and house you left behind were confiscated by the state.
남아서 공화국에 충성을 맹세한다: Stay and swear loyalty to the Republic
무사히 시절을 넘겼습니다: You came through those times safely
You gave up your title and lived as a ‘citizen’. You kept part of the land.
혐의자로 체포되었습니다: You were arrested as a suspect
You spent months in prison and were released only after Thermidor.
시골 영지에 조용히 숨는다: Hide quietly on your country estate
Ahead of the Estates-General, every parish is collecting a cahier de doléances setting out the people's grievances and wishes. People have gathered in the village square.
불만을 적어 넣자고 나선다: Step forward and have the grievances written in
You had taxes, corvées and the price of bread written into the cahier.
글을 아는 사람에게 맡긴다: Leave it to someone who can write
You watched as the notary wrote it out for you.
괜히 나섰다가 화를 입을까 빠진다: Keep out of it, in case speaking up brings trouble
삼부회를 앞두고 파리의 60개 선거구마다 진정서를 모읍니다. 당신 구역의: Ahead of the Estates-General, each of the sixty electoral districts of Paris is collecting a cahier. Your district's assembly meets in the church.
삼부회를 앞두고 {고향}의 동업 조합과 교구마다 진정서를 모읍니다. 조합: Ahead of the Estates-General, every guild and parish in {고향} is collecting a cahier. The masters have gathered in the guild hall.
영주의 관리인이 밀린 부과조와 방앗간 사용료를 내라고 합니다. 올해 수확: The lord's agent demands the arrears of dues and the fee for using the mill. This year's harvest will barely cover it.
빚을 내서라도 낸다: Pay, even if you have to borrow
You borrowed money and paid the dues.
마을 사람들과 함께 영주 법정에 호소한다: Appeal to the seigneurial court with the other villagers
Errors turned up in the old registers, and part of the dues was struck off.
It only cost you the legal fees.
You were not found out, but your conscience is uneasy.
교회와 망명 귀족에게서 몰수한 땅이 경매에 나왔습니다. 아시냐 지폐로 값: Land confiscated from the Church and from émigré nobles has come up for auction. It can be paid for in assignats.
You bought fields and vineyards that had belonged to a monastery. Rents will come in from now on.
소유권 다툼에 휘말렸습니다: You were caught up in a dispute over ownership
A quarrel broke out with the old tenants. The neighbours look at you askance too.
It weighed on your conscience, and you did not go to the auction.
빵값이 하루가 다르게 오릅니다. 여자들이 앞장서서 곡물 창고로 몰려가며: The price of bread rises by the day. Women lead the crowd to the granary, shouting for it to be sold at the ‘just price’.
함께 곡물 창고로 간다: Go to the granary with them
정당한 값에 곡물을 샀습니다: You bought grain at a just price
In the end the merchant handed over his wheat at the price the crowd set.
기마 경찰대에 붙잡혔습니다: You were seized by the mounted constabulary
You were held for a few days and then released.
You held out by putting less bread in the soup.
동업조합의 장인이 되려면 걸작을 만들어 심사를 받고 큰 가입금을 내야 합: To become a master in the guild you must make a masterpiece, have it judged, and pay a large entry fee. It is far easier for a master's son or son-in-law.
걸작을 만들어 심사를 받는다: Make a masterpiece and submit it
The examiners nodded. Now you can open your own workshop.
They picked on a tiny flaw. You lost the entry fee for nothing.
You work in someone else's workshop for wages.
내 작업장을 열까?: Open a workshop of your own?
동업조합이 폐지되어 영업세만 내면 누구나 가게를 열 수 있습니다. 경쟁자: The guilds have been abolished, and anyone who pays the licence tax can open a shop. There are just as many more competitors.
You hung up a small sign. You even took on an apprentice.
There were too few customers, and you closed the shop the following year.
남의 작업장에서 계속 일한다: Keep working in someone else's workshop
갓난아기를 시골 유모에게 보낼까?: Send the baby to a wet nurse in the country?
도시의 많은 집이 일하느라 갓난아기를 시골 유모에게 맡깁니다. 비용이 들: Many town households, busy with work, put their newborns out to wet nurses in the country. It costs money, and you will not see the child for several years.
시골 유모에게 맡긴다: Put the baby out to a country wet nurse
아이를 마차에 태워 보냈습니다. 일은 계속할 수 있지만 마음이 무겁습니다: You sent the baby off in a cart. You can keep working, but your heart is heavy.
집에서 직접 키운다: Raise the baby yourself at home
You cut back on work and raise the child at your side.
나폴레옹이 영국과의 무역을 금지했습니다. 설탕과 커피값이 치솟고, 항구에: Napoleon has forbidden trade with Britain. The price of sugar and coffee is soaring, and there is talk of smuggling in the ports.
Under cover of darkness you brought in English goods. Your strongbox grew heavy.
세관에 적발되었습니다: You were caught by the customs men
The goods were seized and you were fined.
사탕무 설탕 같은 새 사업에 투자한다: Invest in a new business such as beet sugar
You bought a share in a beet-sugar works of the kind the government encourages.
규정을 지키며 버틴다: Keep to the rules and hold out
Trade fell off, but your conscience is clear.
재산을 어떻게 물려줄까: How to pass on your property
공증인을 불러 유언장을 쓸 때가 되었습니다. 민법전 이후로는 자녀들에게: It is time to call the notary and make your will. Since the Civil Code, children must share alike, but they say there are ways to leave more to the eldest.
자녀들에게 똑같이 나눈다: Divide it equally among your children
모두에게 같은 몫을 남겼습니다. 땅은 잘게 나뉘겠지만 다툼은 없을 것입니: You left everyone the same share. The land will be cut into small pieces, but there will be no quarrels.
집과 땅은 맏이에게, 나머지는 돈으로: The house and land to the eldest, the rest in money
You decided to keep the family home together. The younger ones are hurt.
일부를 교구와 가난한 이웃에게 남긴다: Leave part to the parish and the poor of the neighbourhood
You cut the children's shares a little and promised a gift to charity.
공증인을 불러 유언장을 쓸 때가 되었습니다. 혁명은 장자 상속을 없앴습니: It is time to call the notary and make your will. The Revolution abolished primogeniture. Divide the château and the estates equally among the children, and the family's lands will be in pieces within a generation.
공증인을 불러 유언장을 쓸 때가 되었습니다. 가게와 국채, 셋집 두 채를: It is time to call the notary and make your will. You weigh how to divide the shop, the government bonds and the two rented houses, and whether, within the Civil Code's reserved shares, you can leave more to the eldest.
공증인을 불러 유언장을 쓸 때가 되었습니다. 민법전대로 땅을 자식들에게: It is time to call the notary and make your will. Divide the land equally among the children as the Civil Code says, and each share will be the size of a palm. Many families give the house and land to the eldest and have them pay the others in money.
자녀 집으로 들어갈까?: Move in with one of your children?
혼자 살림을 꾸리기가 버거워졌습니다. 자녀가 함께 살자고 합니다. 대신: Running a household alone has become too much. One of your children asks you to come and live with them. There is also talk of handing over the land and house in advance.
재산을 넘기고 자녀 집에 들어간다: Hand over your property and move in with your child
You signed a maintenance contract and moved into your child's house. The grandchildren are always around you.
내 집에서 혼자 지낸다: Live alone in your own house
You decided to stay in the house you know. A neighbour looks in from time to time.
혼자 밭과 살림을 꾸리기가 버거워졌습니다. 자녀가 ‘생전 증여’ 계약을: Running the fields and the household alone has become too much. One of your children proposes a ‘gift between the living’: a notarised contract in which you hand over the land and house now, and in return they feed and clothe you until you die.
혼자 살림을 꾸리기가 버거워졌습니다. 자녀가 자기 좁은 셋방으로 들어오라: Running a household alone has become too much. One of your children asks you to move into their cramped rented room. There is talk that in return you should hand over your remaining goods and tools.
혼자 집안을 꾸리기가 버거워졌습니다. 자녀가 함께 살자고 합니다. 공증인: Running the household alone has become too much. One of your children asks you to come and live with them. The notary hints that you could also sell the house for a life annuity, en viager, to provide for your old age.
배우자를 떠나보낸 지 시간이 흘렀습니다. 이웃이 비슷한 처지의 사람을 소: Time has passed since you lost your spouse. A neighbour offers to introduce you to someone in the same situation.
조용히 재혼했습니다. 마을 젊은이들이 밤에 냄비를 두드리며 놀려 댔습니다: You remarried quietly. The village young people banged pots under your windows at night to mock you: a charivari.
You decided to live alone with your memories.
남편을 떠나보낸 지 한 해가 지났습니다. 이웃이 아내를 잃은 홀아비 하나: A year has passed since you lost your husband. A neighbour offers to introduce you to a widower who has lost his wife. If you remarry, the guardianship of the children and the share your first husband left will have to be settled again.
아내를 떠나보낸 지 한 해가 지났습니다. 아이들을 돌볼 사람이 필요하다며: A year has passed since you lost your wife. Saying you need someone to look after the children, a neighbour offers to introduce you to a widow of the village.
살아온 이야기를 적을까?: Write down the story of your life?
젊은 사람들이 옛날이야기를 청합니다. 당신이 겪은 시대를 기록으로 남길: The young ask for stories of the old days. Few people are left who could put on record the times you lived through.
가족 기록장(livre de raison)에 적는다: Write it in the family book, the livre de raison
Every evening by candlelight you wrote down the years gone by.
You sat the grandchildren on your knee and told them stories of the old days.
늙기 전에 이름난 성지에 다녀오고 싶다는 마음이 듭니다. 걸어서 몇 주가: You want to visit a famous shrine before you grow old. It is a road of several weeks on foot.
Leaning on a stick, you made the journey to the shrine. Your body is worn out, but your heart is light.
You prayed quietly in the place you know.
법학부에서 몇 해 공부하고 학위를 사면 변호사가 될 수 있습니다. 돈이: Study a few years in a faculty of law and buy a degree, and you can become an advocate. It costs money and you need connections, but in these times the law is the short road to getting on.
법학부에 등록한다: Enrol in the faculty of law
법률 서기로 시작 / 학비에 막힘: Start as a law clerk / stopped by the fees
법률 사무소에 들어갔습니다: You went into a law office
랭스에서 학위를 받고 공증인 사무소의 서기로 일을 시작했습니다. 첫 소송: You took your degree at Reims and began as a clerk in a notary's office. You stay up nights copying your first case papers.
학비를 감당하지 못했습니다: You could not meet the fees
You gave up your studies after two years. Still, you learned how to read a law code.
You gave up the dream of the law.
인쇄소에서 교정 볼 사람을 구합니다. 팸플릿과 신문이 쏟아지는 도시에서는: A print shop is looking for a proofreader. In a city awash with pamphlets and newspapers, a road is opening for people who write.
인쇄소 교정원으로 들어간다: Go into the print shop as a proofreader
잉크 냄새 나는 인쇄소에서 활자를 고르고 남의 글을 고칩니다. 언젠가 내: In a print shop that smells of ink you sort type and correct other people's writing. You wait for the day your own will be printed.
가문의 아들로서 국왕의 군대에 소위로 들어갈 수 있습니다. 1781년 법: As a son of the family you can enter the king's army as a sub-lieutenant. Since the ordinance of 1781, an officer must prove four generations of nobility.
연대에 소위로 들어간다: Join a regiment as a sub-lieutenant
You put on the white uniform and were posted to your regiment.
You left the soldier's road to another brother.
흰 군복을 입고 연대에 배치되었습니다. 포병 학교 시험에서는 아카데미의: You put on the white uniform and were posted to your regiment. At the artillery school examination, the examiner was the Academy's young mathematician, Laplace.
황제가 세운 생시르 특별 군사학교가 입학생을 받습니다. 학비를 내야 하지: The special military school the Emperor founded at Saint-Cyr is taking cadets. There are fees to pay, but graduates are commissioned as sub-lieutenants straight away.
For two years you learned drill, gunnery and mathematics, and you were commissioned as a sub-lieutenant.
You decided not to put on a uniform.
선생님이 당신의 수학 실력이 범상치 않다며, 학자의 길을 권합니다. 17: Your teacher says your mathematics is out of the ordinary and urges you towards a scholar's life. After 1794 you could sit the entrance examination for the new École polytechnique.
수학 교사로 시작 / 기회 없음: Start as a mathematics teacher / no opening
사관학교 예비반에서 수학을 가르치며 아카데미에 보낼 논문을 쓰기 시작했습: Teaching mathematics in a preparatory class for the military schools, you began writing a paper to send to the Academy.
You found no post. Every night you read mathematics books alone.
You buried your gift in your heart.
이름난 화가의 작업실에서 제자를 받는다고 합니다. 몇 해 동안 물감을 개: A well-known painter's studio is taking pupils. For years you would grind colours and draw plaster casts, but one day you might hang a picture at the Salon.
작업실 구석에서 석고상을 그리며 하루를 보냅니다. 스승은 좀처럼 칭찬하지: You spend the day in a corner of the studio drawing plaster casts. The master rarely gives praise.
You put the sketchbook away in a drawer.
상점 점원 자리: A place as a shop assistant
도매상 한 곳에서 계산이 빠른 점원을 구합니다. 장부와 편지를 쓸 줄 알: A wholesale merchant is looking for an assistant who is quick with figures. Better still if you can keep books and write letters.
계산대 뒤에서 손님을 맞고 장부를 씁니다. 언젠가 내 가게를 열 날을 꿈: Behind the counter you serve customers and keep the books. You dream of the day you open a shop of your own.
You chose the work you know.
수녀원 원장이 당신을 눈여겨보았습니다. 수녀원은 기도뿐 아니라 학교와 병: The mother superior has taken notice of you. A convent is not only for prayer; it runs schools and hospitals too. She says they would take you even with a small dowry.
머리를 가리고 수련복을 입었습니다. 새벽 기도와 아이들 수업으로 하루가: You covered your hair and put on the novice's habit. Your days are filled with dawn prayers and teaching children.
You took your leave of the mother superior as you went out through the convent gate.
외과의는 오랫동안 이발사와 한 동업조합에 묶여 천대받았지만, 군대와 병원: Surgeons were long looked down on, bound in one guild with the barbers, but the army and the hospitals are always short of them. From 1794 medicine is taught at the national schools of health too.
해부실과 병원 병동을 오가며 붕대 감는 법부터 배웁니다. 피 냄새에 익숙: Going back and forth between the dissecting room and the hospital wards, you learn, starting with how to bind a dressing. It took months to get used to the smell of blood.
Medicine will have to wait for another life.
영국식 방적기와 직기를 들여와 사람을 고용해 돌리는 작업장이 늘고 있습니: More and more workshops bring in English-style spinning machines and looms and hire people to run them. It needs capital, but if it goes well it means a fortune.
기계를 들여 작업장을 연다: Bring in machines and open a works
중고 방적기 몇 대와 직공 열 명으로 시작했습니다. 기계가 멈출 때마다: You started with a few second-hand spinning machines and ten workers. Every time a machine stops, your heart sinks.
You decided to leave the risk to others.
관청 서기 자리: A place as a government clerk
새로 생긴 데파르트망과 부처마다 서류를 쓸 사람이 필요합니다. 글씨가 반: Every new département and ministry needs people to write documents. They say that if your handwriting is neat, you can get in.
소매 토시를 끼고 하루 종일 공문을 베껴 씁니다. 월급은 적지만 꼬박꼬박: Wearing sleeve protectors, you copy official letters all day. The pay is small, but it comes without fail.
You declined the piles of paper.
마을 학교에 교사가 없습니다. 읽기와 쓰기, 교리 문답과 셈을 가르치면: The village school has no teacher. Teaching reading and writing, the catechism and sums, you would collect a little fee from each family. After 1833 the commune pays a salary too.
나무 의자와 석판 몇 개뿐인 교실에서 아이들을 만났습니다. 겨울에는 아이: You met the children in a classroom with nothing but wooden benches and a few slates. In winter each child brings a log for the stove.
You decided that teaching children was not for you.
구의 학교에 보조 교사 자리가 났습니다. 읽기와 쓰기, 교리 문답과 셈을: A post as assistant teacher has come up at the district school. Teaching reading and writing, the catechism and sums, you would be paid a small salary by the city.
{고향}의 학교에 보조 교사 자리가 났습니다. 읽기와 쓰기, 교리 문답과: A post as assistant teacher has come up at a school in {고향}. Teaching reading and writing, the catechism and sums, you would be paid a small salary.
마을에 들른 유랑 극단이 단원을 구합니다. 배우는 교회에서 파문당하는 직: A company of strolling players passing through is looking for members. Actors are excommunicated by the Church, and your parents would be up in arms, but applause is sweet.
수레를 타고 이 도시 저 도시를 떠돕니다. 첫 무대에서 대사를 잊었지만: You wander from town to town in a wagon. You forgot your lines at your first performance, but the audience laughed kindly.
You watched the players' wagon leave.
일주일에 한 번 집을 열어 작가와 정치가, 학자를 맞는 ‘살롱’은 이 시: A ‘salon’, where once a week you open your house to writers, politicians and scholars, is one of the few roads by which a woman of this age reaches the public world.
첫 모임에는 손님이 넷뿐이었습니다. 대화가 무르익자 자정이 넘어서야 끝났: Only four guests came to the first gathering. Once the conversation warmed up, it went on past midnight.
You kept the house a space for the family alone.
서랍에 쌓인 원고를 출판업자에게 보여 줄 수도 있습니다. 대부분은 돌아오: You could show the manuscripts piling up in your drawer to a publisher. Most come back, but now and then a book shakes the world.
출판업자는 “나쁘지 않다”고 말했습니다. 자비로 300부를 찍기로 했습니: The publisher said it was “not bad”. You agreed to print three hundred copies at your own expense.
원고를 서랍에 둔다: Leave the manuscript in the drawer
You thought the time was not yet right.
마을의 늙은 산파가 뒤를 이을 사람을 찾습니다. 출산은 여자들 사이의 일: The village's old midwife is looking for someone to take her place. Childbirth is women's business, and the midwife is one of the most trusted people in the village.
한밤중에 불려 나가 물을 끓이고 아기를 받았습니다. 첫 울음소리에 눈물이: Called out in the middle of the night, you boiled water and delivered a baby. At its first cry, you wept.
You did not feel able to carry that weight.
구의 늙은 산파가 뒤를 이을 사람을 찾습니다. 시립 산과 학교에서 자격을: The district's old midwife is looking for someone to take her place. With a certificate from the city school of midwifery you can become a licensed midwife.
{고향}의 늙은 산파가 뒤를 이을 사람을 찾습니다. 출산은 여자들 사이의: The old midwife of {고향} is looking for someone to take her place. Childbirth is women's business, and the midwife is one of the most trusted people in the neighbourhood.
리본과 레이스, 모자를 파는 의상실에서 견습 재봉사를 구합니다. 손이 빠: A shop selling ribbons, lace and hats is looking for an apprentice seamstress. Quick hands and a good eye could mean a shop of your own one day.
바늘에 손가락을 여러 번 찔렸습니다. 주인은 당신의 리본 매듭이 예쁘다고: You pricked your fingers on the needle many times. The mistress said your ribbon bows were pretty.
You decided to sew only at home.
항구에 상선과 어선이 드나듭니다. 견습 선원으로 올라타면 세상의 끝까지: Merchant ships and fishing boats come and go in the harbour. Sign on as a ship's boy and you could go to the ends of the earth, but many never come back.
첫 항해에서 내내 뱃멀미를 했습니다. 갑판장이 웃으며 밧줄 매는 법을 가: You were seasick for the whole of your first voyage. The boatswain laughed and taught you how to tie knots.
You decided to live with only the sound of the waves.
몽주가 세운 이공대학이 시험만으로 학생을 뽑습니다. 출신은 묻지 않고,: The École polytechnique founded by Monge chooses its students by examination alone. It does not ask where you come from, and if you pass, the state pays your fees. Graduates go into civil engineering, the mines and the artillery.
군복 같은 교복을 입고 몽주의 화법기하학 강의를 들었습니다. 졸업 뒤 토: Wearing a uniform-like school coat, you attended Monge's lectures on descriptive geometry. After graduating you were posted to the Corps of Bridges and Roads.
You decided to try again the following year. You opened your mathematics books once more.
You decided to take another road.
경찰 순경 자리: A place as a police constable
제1통령 아래 새로 짜인 경찰이 사람을 뽑습니다. 정보원을 부리고 술집과: The police, newly organised under the First Consul, are recruiting. The work is running informers and keeping an eye on taverns and lodging houses.
You were issued a blue uniform. People in the neighbourhood now watch their words in front of you.
You had no stomach for spying on your neighbours.
수녀들의 자선학교에 보내 달라고 할까?: Ask to go to the sisters' charity school?
이웃집 여자아이가 애덕 수녀회가 여는 자선학교에 다니기 시작했습니다. 교:
The neighbours' daughter has started going to a charity school run by the Daughters of Charity. They teach the catechism, reading and sewing, she says.
Your father says that for a girl, sewing and housework come before letters. Your mother has said she will hear what you have to ask.
부모에게 자선학교에 보내 달라고 부탁한다: Ask your parents to send you to the charity school
자선학교에 다니게 되었습니다: You went to the charity school
Your mother talked your father round. You learn the catechism and reading from the sisters. They teach only a little writing.
“여자아이가 글을 배워 무엇에 쓰겠느냐.” 아버지의 말에 더는 조르지 못: “What use is reading to a girl?” After your father said that, you could not ask again.
바느질 학교만 허락받았습니다: You were allowed only the sewing school
읽기 대신 바느질 학교에 다니기로 했습니다. 수놓는 틈틈이 기도서의 글자: Instead of reading, you went to a sewing school. Between stitches you picked up a few letters from the prayer book.
어머니에게 기도서 읽는 법을 배운다: Learn to read the prayer book from your mother
조금씩 읽기 / 시간이 없음: Reading bit by bit / no time
기도서를 더듬더듬 읽게 되었습니다: You came to stumble through the prayer book
저녁마다 어머니와 기도서를 펼쳤습니다. 쓰는 법은 모르지만 읽을 수는 있: Every evening you opened the prayer book with your mother. You cannot write, but you can read.
어머니에게 그럴 여유가 없었습니다: Your mother had no time to spare
Your mother had too much work as well, and after a few tries it stopped.
집안일과 작업장 심부름을 돕는다: Help with the housework and run errands for the workshop
가업 경험 / 교육 기회 감소: Experience of the trade / fewer chances to study
집안의 일손이 되었습니다: You became a pair of hands for the household
물을 긷고 동생을 돌보고 작업장 심부름을 합니다. 실 감는 손이 어른만큼: You fetch water, look after the little ones and run errands for the workshop. Your hands wind thread as fast as a grown-up's.
겨울이 되면 성당지기의 아내가 마을 여자아이 몇을 모아 교리 문답과 기도: When winter comes, the sexton's wife gathers a few village girls to teach them the catechism, reading from the prayer book, and spinning. It is held apart from the boys' school.
겨울 동안 배움 / 일손이 필요함: Learning through the winter / hands needed at home
난롯가에 앉아 기도문을 외우고 글자를 짚어 가며 읽었습니다. 봄이 되자: Sitting by the stove, you learned prayers by heart and read the letters one by one with your finger. In spring you helped in the fields again.
집에 일손이 필요하다고 했습니다: They said hands were needed at home
You had to look after the little ones and work the spinning wheel.
어머니 곁에서 실 잣기를 배운다: Learn to spin at your mother's side
물레 돌리는 법을 익혔습니다. 겨울밤 마실에서 어른들이 솜씨를 칭찬했습니: You learned to work the spinning wheel. At the winter veillée the grown-ups praised your skill.
부모는 당신을 우르술라회 수녀원 기숙학교에 보낼지 고민합니다. 교리와 예: Your parents are wondering whether to send you to the Ursulines' convent boarding school. You would learn the catechism and manners, reading and writing, embroidery and music. Unlike a collège, it does not teach Latin.
프랑스어 작문과 자수로 상을 받았습니다. 몇몇 친구와는 평생 편지를 주고: You won prizes for French composition and embroidery. With some of your friends you will exchange letters all your life.
The discipline was strict and the winters cold. Still, you learned to read and write.
집에서 어머니와 가정교사에게 배운다: Learn at home from your mother and a governess
At your mother's side you learned housekeeping and manners, reading and writing.
가문의 딸을 어떻게 가르칠까: How to educate a daughter of the family
가문의 딸에게 맞는 교육을 정할 때입니다. 1793년까지는 가난한 귀족: It is time to choose an education fit for a daughter of the family. Until 1793 there is also the royal school for girls at Saint-Cyr, which takes daughters of poor noble families.
From a governess you learn French and Italian, the harp and drawing.
생시르 왕립 여학교에 지원한다: Apply to the royal school at Saint-Cyr
엄격한 규율 속에 역사와 지리, 음악을 배웁니다. 스무 살이 되면 지참금: Under strict discipline you learn history, geography and music. At twenty you will leave with a dowry.
Your recommendations were not enough. You were sent to a convent boarding school instead.
어머니 곁에서 예법을 배운다: Learn manners at your mother's side
You learned the manners of the salon and the art of letter-writing from your mother.
두 분 모두 떠나시고, 형제자매가 공증인 사무실에 모였습니다. 집과 밭,: Both parents are gone, and the brothers and sisters have gathered at the notary's office. The house and fields, a few pieces of furniture and the papers of debts lie on the table.
고르게 나눔 / 땅이 너무 잘게 쪼개짐: Fair shares / the land cut too fine
You drew lots for the shares and signed without a quarrel.
땅이 너무 잘게 쪼개졌습니다: The land was cut too fine
각자 받은 밭이 너무 작아 농사를 지어도 먹고살기 어렵습니다. 결국 몇몇: Each field received is too small to live on by farming. In the end some of you sold their land and left for the town.
내가 집을 맡고 형제들 몫은 돈으로 갚는다: Take the house yourself and pay the others in money
집을 지킴 / 빚이 무거움: Keeping the house / a heavy debt
You took on the house, promising to pay your brothers and sisters over several years.
When a bad year came you could not pay on time as promised, and there were hard words with your siblings.
형제들에게 양보한다: Give way to your brothers and sisters
형제들이 고마워했습니다: Your brothers and sisters were grateful
You gave your share to a brother or sister in need.
손에 남은 것이 없습니다: Nothing was left in your hands
Later, when times grew hard, you regretted that decision a little.
두 분 모두 떠나시고, 형제자매가 공증인 사무실에 모였습니다. 셋방의 가: Both parents are gone, and the brothers and sisters have gathered at the notary's office. A few pieces of furniture from the rented rooms, the workshop tools and the papers of debts lie on the table.
두 분 모두 떠나시고, 형제자매가 공증인 사무실에 모였습니다. {고향}의: Both parents are gone, and the brothers and sisters have gathered at the notary's office. A house in {고향}, the shop fittings and the papers of debts lie on the table.
혼자서는 살림을 꾸리기 어려워진 부모님이 함께 살 수 있겠느냐고 조심스럽: Your parents, who can no longer manage a household alone, ask cautiously whether they could live with you.
함께한 마지막 몇 해 / 살림이 빠듯함: The last years together / a tight household
The grandchildren gather round their grandparents to hear stories of the old days.
Nursing them every night wore you out, and you quarrelled with your spouse more often.
They found places in a hospice run by nuns. You visit every Sunday.
It was a ward where several people shared a narrow bed. It stayed on your mind for a long time.
이웃에게 돈을 주고 돌봐 달라고 한다: Pay a neighbour to look after them
You paid the widow next door each month to look after your parents.
혼자서는 밭일도 살림도 어려워진 부모님이 함께 살 수 있겠느냐고 조심스럽: Your parents, who can no longer manage the fields or the household alone, ask cautiously whether they could live with you. A bed beside the kitchen would do, they say.
혼자서는 계단을 오르내리기도 어려워진 부모님이 함께 살 수 있겠느냐고 조: Your parents, who can hardly manage the stairs alone any more, ask cautiously whether they could live with you. Your rented rooms are already cramped.
Your brothers and sisters discuss how to care for parents who can no longer run their house alone. The cost of one more maid is no small thing.
다 자란 자녀에게 혼담이 들어왔습니다. 상대 집안은 지참금 이야기부터 꺼: An offer of marriage has come for your grown child. The other family starts by talking about the dowry.
지참금을 마련해 혼인시킨다: Find the dowry and marry them off
The marriage contract was signed and a feast was held. Your child left for a new home.
지참금 때문에 빚을 졌습니다: The dowry put you in debt
You overreached to keep up appearances. You spent years paying off the debt.
자녀가 원하는 사람과 하게 둔다: Let them marry the person they want
행복한 혼인 / 집안의 체면: A happy marriage / the family's standing
자녀가 원하는 사람과 혼인했습니다: Your child married the person they wanted
They have nothing, but they cherish each other.
“To marry into a family like that!” You heard the talk for some time.
아직은 집에 둔다: Keep them at home for now
You put off the match. Your child seems disappointed.
아들이 스무 살이 되어 징병 추첨에 나갑니다. 돈이 있는 집은 대리인을: Your son has turned twenty and goes to draw in the conscription lottery. Families with money buy a substitute to go into the army in their son's place.
You emptied your savings to pay a young man from a poor family to enlist in your son's place. His face stayed with you for a long time.
Your son came home smiling. That evening the whole family lit a candle in church.
Your son put on the uniform and left for his regiment. He waved from the doorway for a long time.
The mayor came to the door with a letter. It came from your son's regiment.
“어머니, 아버지, 저는 잘 지냅니다.” 서툰 글씨였지만 분명 아들의 글: “Mother, Father, I am well.” The handwriting was clumsy, but it was surely your son's.
아들이 다리를 다쳐 귀향한다는 소식입니다. 살아 돌아온다는 것만으로 감사: The news is that your son has been wounded in the leg and is coming home. That he is coming back alive was enough to be thankful for.
“Fighting bravely…” After that, the letters would not come into focus.
1792년부터 법이 이혼을 허락합니다. 몇 해째 남남처럼 지내는 배우자와: From 1792 the law allows divorce. You wonder whether to go on living like this with a spouse who has been a stranger to you for years.
새 출발 / 집안의 비난: A fresh start / the family's reproach
The divorce was posted at the town hall. The neighbours whispered, but you could breathe again.
The priest and your relatives called divorce a sin. You were lonely for years.
조금씩 다시 가까워졌습니다: Little by little you grew close again
You went to market together and ate supper together, and began to talk again.
You live under one roof, in separate rooms.
1792년부터 구청에서 이혼을 받아 줍니다. 파리에서는 몇 해 사이 혼인: From 1792 the district office accepts divorces. In Paris, they say, about one couple in five married in recent years has separated. You wonder whether to go on living like this with a spouse who has been a stranger to you for years.
1792년부터 법이 이혼을 허락한다지만, 마을에서 이혼한 사람은 아직 아: The law has allowed divorce since 1792, they say, but no one in the village has ever been divorced. The priest says it is a sin, and the neighbours would whisper for the rest of your life. You wonder whether to go on living like this with a spouse who has been a stranger to you for years.
1792년부터 이혼이 가능하지만, 이혼하면 지참금과 공동 재산을 나누는: Divorce has been possible since 1792, but it brings a lawsuit over dividing the dowry and the joint property. You wonder whether to go on living like this with a spouse who has been a stranger to you for years.
형제자매 한 사람이 병으로 세상을 떠나고 어린 조카만 남았습니다. 누군가: One of your brothers or sisters has died of illness, leaving only a young child. Someone has to take them in.
새 식구 / 먹일 입 하나 더: A new member of the family / one more mouth to feed
조카가 새 식구가 되었습니다: The child became one of the family
Silent at first, the child began to smile after a few months.
There were frequent fights between the child and your own children.
수도회 고아원에 맡긴다: Leave them at a convent orphanage
You left the child with the orphanage sisters. Your relatives' looks stung.
장인에게 도제로 맡긴다: Place them as apprentice to a craftsman
You sent the child as apprentice to a craftsman you know. Bed and board are settled.
갓난아기를 먹일 것이 없습니다. 도시의 가난한 집들 가운데는 아이를 기아: There is nothing to feed the newborn. Among the poor households of the town, not a few leave a child in the turning wheel at the door of the foundling hospital. In Paris at the end of the eighteenth century, about a third of all children born were left that way.
아이를 품에 두었습니다: You kept the child in your arms
Neighbour women shared their milk and brought old clothes.
All through the depth of winter the whole family went hungry.
아이를 보호소에 맡긴다: Leave the child at the foundling hospital
밤에 회전함에 아이를 넣고 종을 울렸습니다. 아이의 이름을 적은 쪽지와: At night you put the child in the wheel and rang the bell. With the child you left a note with its name and half of a medal. You hope to find it one day.
아무 표식도 남기지 못했습니다: You could not leave any token
In your haste you put in neither note nor medal.
시골 유모에게 보낸다: Send the child to a country wet nurse
빚을 내 시골 유모에게 아이를 보냈습니다. 몇 달에 한 번 소식을 듣습니: You borrowed money and sent the child to a wet nurse in the country. You hear news once every few months.
맡긴 아이를 찾아서: Looking for the child you left
형편이 조금 나아졌습니다. 보호소에 맡긴 아이를 찾아갈 수 있을지, 그: Things have got a little better. The thought will not leave you: could you go and find the child you left at the foundling hospital?
보호소 기록을 찾아간다: Go and search the hospital's records
시골 위탁 가정에서 자란 아이를 만났습니다. 아이는 당신을 알아보지 못했: You met the child, raised by a foster family in the country. They did not recognise you, but the half medal fitted exactly.
The register said the child died with the foster family a few months after being left. Most children left at the hospital never lived to their first birthday.
Too many children had been left on the same day.
아이의 삶을 흔들고 싶지 않았습니다. 해마다 그날이 오면 성당에 초를 켭: You did not want to upset the child's life. Every year, when that day comes, you light a candle in church.
아이를 가졌습니다. 아이 아버지는 혼인을 약속했지만 요즘 들어 얼굴을 보: You are with child. The father promised to marry you, but lately he is hard to find. Before the Revolution the law required a declaration of pregnancy, and the world is harsh to an unmarried mother.
아이 아버지에게 혼인을 요구한다: Demand that the father marry you
두 집안이 서둘러 혼인 날짜를 잡았습니다. 몇 달 뒤 아이가 태어났습니다: The two families hurriedly set a wedding date. A few months later the child was born.
그는 다른 도시로 떠났습니다. 혼자 아이를 낳아 키웁니다. 성당에서도 시: He left for another town. You bear and raise the child alone. At church and at market alike, people whisper behind your back.
도시로 가서 몰래 아이를 낳는다: Go to the town and give birth in secret
아이를 낳고 돌아왔습니다: You had the child and came back
도시의 산과 병원에서 아이를 낳았습니다. 아이는 시골 유모에게 맡기고 매: You gave birth at the town's lying-in hospital. The child is with a country wet nurse, and you send money every month.
아이를 보호소에 남겼습니다: You left the child at the foundling hospital
You came back alone. You told no one.
아이를 낳아 혼자 키운다: Have the child and raise it alone
You held your head up and had the child. Your mother, at least, was on your side.
아이를 가졌습니다. 하녀로 일하는 집 아들이 혼인을 약속했지만, 마님은: You are with child. The son of the house where you work as a maid promised to marry you, but his mother thinks only of how to put you out. The world is harsh to an unmarried mother.
아이를 가졌습니다. 마을 축제 뒤로 아이 아버지는 혼인을 약속했지만 요즘: You are with child. After the village fête the father promised to marry you, but lately he is hard to find. The village is harsh to an unmarried mother.
노예선 투자: A share in a slave ship
상인 동료가 아프리카 해안을 거쳐 생도맹그로 가는 배의 지분을 사라고 권: A fellow merchant urges you to buy a share in a ship sailing by way of the African coast to Saint-Domingue. The ship buys people, loads them aboard and crosses the Atlantic. Many families in Bordeaux and Nantes built their fortunes this way.
큰 이익 / 배를 잃음: A large profit / the ship is lost
배가 돌아왔고 이익이 났습니다: The ship returned and made a profit
항해가 끝나고 배당금이 들어왔습니다. 장부에는 ‘화물’이라고만 적혀 있습: The voyage ended and the dividend came in. The ledger says only ‘cargo’. You did not read the report that many of the people aboard died on the crossing.
배가 영국 군함에 나포되었거나 반란이 일어났다고 합니다. 투자금은 돌아오: They say the ship was taken by a British warship, or there was a revolt aboard. The money invested never came back.
“사람을 사고파는 일에는 손대지 않겠습니다.” 동료는 어깨를 으쓱했습니다: “I will have nothing to do with buying and selling people.” Your colleague shrugged.
상인들 사이에서 따돌림을 받았습니다: You were shunned among the merchants
One by one, your dealings in the port fell away.
사흘째 식구들이 제대로 먹지 못했습니다. 빵집 진열대의 빵이 눈앞에 있습: For three days the family has not eaten properly. The bread on the baker's counter is right in front of you. If you are caught, you could be sent to prison or the galleys (later, the penal colony).
빵을 품에 숨기고 뛰었습니다. 아이들은 배불리 먹었고, 당신은 그날 밤: You hid the bread under your coat and ran. The children ate their fill, and you could not sleep that night.
빵집 주인이 소리를 질렀고 경찰에게 끌려갔습니다. 몇 달을 감옥에서 보냈: The baker shouted, and you were dragged off by the police. You spent months in prison. You could not bring yourself to ask how the family had managed meanwhile.
교구 구호소에 간다: Go to the parish relief office
You stood in line at the relief office and were given a bowl of soup and half a loaf.
You sold the silver spoons you were given as part of your dowry.
구역 감시 위원회 사람이 찾아왔습니다. 이웃 하나가 왕당파라는 진술서에: A man from the section's watch committee has come. He wants you to sign a statement that a neighbour is a royalist. If you do not sign, you may come under suspicion yourself.
며칠 뒤 그 이웃이 끌려갔습니다. 그 집 아이들의 얼굴을 볼 수 없었습니: A few days later the neighbour was taken away. You could not look their children in the face.
위원회 사람은 그냥 돌아갔습니다: The committee man simply went away
The neighbour never knew what you did, but you know.
당신 이름도 명단에 올랐습니다: Your own name went on the list
You were watched for weeks and placed under house arrest for a while.
공포정치가 끝나고, 감옥에서 풀려난 사람들이 돌아왔습니다. 거리에서 그때: The Terror is over, and people released from prison have come home. In the street you meet eyes that remember those days.
말을 꺼내기도 전에 문이 닫혔습니다: The door closed before you could speak
You tried to talk about the past, but that door did not open.
“그때 당신이 서명하지 않았다는 걸 들었습니다.” 이웃이 손을 꼭 잡았습: “I heard you would not sign back then.” The neighbour gripped your hand.
You carried on as if nothing had happened.
씨앗 살 돈조차 없습니다. 읍내의 대금업자가 높은 이자로 돈을 빌려주겠다: You do not even have the money for seed. The moneylender in town offers to lend at high interest.
You signed the IOU and took the money. The interest will grow frighteningly.
You sowed only half the seed. The harvest will be smaller.
월세 낼 돈조차 없습니다. 몽드피에테(공영 전당포)에 맡길 물건도 바닥났: You do not even have the rent. You have run out of things to pawn at the Mont-de-Piété, the public pawnshop. A moneylender in the lane offers to lend at high interest.
월세와 재료값을 낼 돈이 없습니다. {고향}의 대금업자가 높은 이자로 돈: You have no money for the rent or for materials. A moneylender in {고향} offers to lend at high interest.
빚을 갚을 날: The day the debt falls due
대금업자가 집달관을 데리고 왔습니다. 원금에 이자가 두 배로 불어 있습니: The moneylender has come with a bailiff. The interest has doubled the principal.
You scraped together everything you had and paid.
The money fell short, and you had to give up a field.
갚을 수 없다고 버틴다: Hold out, saying you cannot pay
몇 달 유예를 받았습니다: You were given a few months' grace
The moneylender grudgingly agreed to wait.
채무 감옥에 갇혔습니다: You were locked up in debtors' prison
빚을 갚을 때까지 감옥에 갇혔습니다. 가족이 물건을 팔아 꺼내 주었습니다: You were imprisoned until the debt was paid. Your family sold things to get you out.
You packed at night and left for another district. You can never go back.
오랜 친구가 찾아와 사정을 털어놓습니다. 몇 해 안에 꼭 갚겠다며 돈을: An old friend comes to you and pours out their troubles. They ask to borrow money, promising to pay it back within a few years.
You handed over the money without an IOU. Your friend bowed their head again and again.
Your friend said they understood, but after that they rarely came by.
News comes of the friend who borrowed money from you.
이자까지 갚음 / 일부만 / 못 갚음: Repaid with interest / partly / not at all
친구는 그 돈으로 일어섰다며 이자까지 얹어 갚았습니다. 둘 사이는 더 깊: Your friend said that money had set them on their feet and paid it back with interest. You grew closer than ever.
Your friend said times were hard for them too. You decided to let the rest go.
Your friend had already left for another district.
열이 내리지 않고 기침이 멎지 않습니다. 의사를 부를지, 동네 접골사나: The fever will not break and the cough will not stop. You must decide whether to call the doctor, go to the local bonesetter or the herb woman, or go and pray to a saint.
With the medicine and diet the doctor prescribed, you were up in a few weeks.
사혈 뒤 더 쇠약해졌습니다: You were weaker after the bleeding
의사가 세 번이나 피를 뽑았습니다. 열은 내렸지만 한동안 일어서기도 어려: The doctor bled you three times. The fever broke, but for a while you could hardly stand.
You drank a bitter herbal brew and sweated, and the fever went down.
You were ill for several more weeks.
성인의 샘에 기도하러 간다: Go and pray at a saint's spring
마음의 위안 / 길에서 지침: Comfort of mind / worn out on the road
You drank from the spring and lit a candle. Strangely, your strength began to come back little by little.
길에서 더 지쳤습니다: The road wore you out further
Walking a long road while sick left you weaker.
열이 내리지 않고 기침이 멎지 않습니다. 이름난 의사를 부르면 사혈과 관: The fever will not break and the cough will not stop. A famous doctor would bleed and purge you and charge a great deal. The household chaplain suggests having the holy oils ready.
열이 내리지 않고 기침이 멎지 않습니다. 단골 의사는 사혈을 권하고, 약: The fever will not break and the cough will not stop. The family doctor recommends bleeding, and the apothecary sells quinine. Your mother has put a medal of a woman saint under your pillow.
열이 내리지 않고 기침이 멎지 않습니다. 오텔디외 병원에 가면 한 침대에: The fever will not break and the cough will not stop. They say that at the Hôtel-Dieu two or three patients share a bed. The doctor is dear, the herb seller in the lane is cheap, and the church of Sainte-Geneviève is close.
열이 내리지 않고 기침이 멎지 않습니다. 시립 병원은 무료지만 들어가면: The fever will not break and the cough will not stop. The town hospital is free, but rumour says those who go in do not come out. The doctor is dear, the herb seller is cheap, and the church is close.
열이 내리지 않고 기침이 멎지 않습니다. 마을에 의사는 없고, 읍내 외과: The fever will not break and the cough will not stop. There is no doctor in the village, and the surgeon in town is half a day away. The bonesetter and the herb woman are close, and the water of the saint's spring in the woods is said to be good for fevers.
아이가 곧 태어납니다. 마을 산파를 부를지, 도시의 외과의(산과의)를 부: The child will soon be born. You must decide whether to call the village midwife, a surgeon-accoucheur from town, or leave it to your mother and the neighbour women.
순산 / 난산: An easy birth / a hard labour
A healthy child was born into the midwife's hands.
It was a long night. The child lived, and you could not get up for some time.
The accoucheur delivered the child. It cost dear, but it was a relief.
아이가 거꾸로 서 있어 산과의가 집게를 썼습니다. 둘 다 살았지만 몸이: The child was breech, and the accoucheur used forceps. Both of you lived, but the pain lasted a long time.
어머니와 이웃 여자들에게 맡긴다: Leave it to your mother and the neighbour women
Water was boiled in the kitchen and the neighbour women stayed by your side all night.
You lost a lot of blood. The child lived, but you were in bed for weeks.
아이가 곧 태어납니다. 구의 산파를 부를지, 오텔디외 병원의 산과에 갈지: The child will soon be born. You must decide whether to call the district midwife, go to the lying-in ward of the Hôtel-Dieu, or leave it to your mother and the neighbour women.
아이가 곧 태어납니다. 동네 산파를 부를지, {고향}의 외과의(산과의)를: The child will soon be born. You must decide whether to call the local midwife, a surgeon-accoucheur in {고향}, or leave it to your mother and the neighbour women.
일이 끝나면 선술집에 들르는 날이 늘었습니다. 요즘은 아침에도 손이 떨립: More and more days you stop at the tavern after work. These days your hands shake even in the morning.
The first weeks were hard, but now you eat supper with your family.
You held out for a few months, then your friends dragged you back to a seat at the tavern.
The hours at the tavern are your only pleasure.
작업장 동료들과 월요일까지 쉬는 ‘성 월요일’이 잦아졌습니다. 선술집 외: More and more often you and your workmates take ‘Saint Monday’ off as well. Your name grows longer on the tavern slate, and these days your hands shake even in the morning.
장날마다 읍내 술집에서 늦게 돌아옵니다. 가축 판 돈이 반쯤 사라진 날도: Every market day you come home late from the tavern in town. Some days half the money from the livestock is gone. These days your hands shake even in the morning.
병영에서 배운 브랜디가 이제 없으면 잠이 오지 않습니다. 요즘은 아침에도: You cannot sleep now without the brandy you learned to drink in barracks. These days your hands shake even in the morning.
카페에서 거래처 사람들과 마시는 술이 늘었습니다. 계산서 숫자가 틀리는: You drink more and more with business contacts at the café. There are days when the figures on the bill come out wrong.
저녁마다 카페에서 신문을 읽으며 마시는 술이 한 잔에서 다섯 잔이 되었습: The drink you take every evening at the café over the newspapers has gone from one glass to five. These days the hand that holds your pen shakes.
일하다 크게 다쳤습니다. 쉬면 품삯이 끊기고, 계속 일하면 몸이 더 상할: You were badly hurt at work. Rest and your wages stop; keep working and your body may suffer worse.
Your body healed, but the debts grew meanwhile.
제자리에 맞춤 / 평생 절뚝임: Set right / a limp for life
The bonesetter set the bone in one go. It hurt enough to make you scream, but it healed.
평생 절뚝이게 되었습니다: You were left with a limp for life
참고 일을 계속한다: Grit your teeth and keep working
You worked through it with clenched teeth. That injury ached into your old age.
작업장에서 크게 다쳤습니다. 기계(직기)에 손이 끼었습니다. 쉬면 품삯이: You were badly hurt in the workshop: your hand was caught in the machine (the loom). Rest and your wages stop, and masters do not wait long for an injured journeyman.
추수 때 낫에 다리를 크게 베었습니다. 쉬면 밭일이 밀리고, 계속 일하면: At harvest you cut your leg badly with the scythe. Rest and the field work piles up; keep working and the wound may get worse.
창고에서 짐을 내리다 허리를 크게 다쳤습니다. 가게를 닫으면 단골이 떨어: You badly hurt your back unloading goods in the warehouse. Close the shop and the regulars drift away; keep standing and you may make it worse.
힘없는 의뢰인이 지역 유력자를 상대로 소송을 맡아 달라고 합니다. 이기면: A client with no influence asks you to take a case against a local magnate. Win and you will make a name, but you will make enemies too.
In court you cross-examined the magnate's witness. The public gallery stirred.
You decided to take only safe briefs.
경찰이 지난 호의 기사를 문제 삼아 경고장을 보냈습니다. 다음에는 신문을: The police have sent a warning over an article in the last issue. Next time, they say, the paper will be suspended.
다음 호에서도 같은 목소리를 냈습니다. 독자는 늘었고 벌금 고지서도 왔습: The next issue spoke with the same voice. Readers multiplied, and so did the fines.
You cut the political articles and ran more serialised novels.
스페인(또는 식민지) 주둔군으로 가면 한 계급 올려 주겠다는 제안이 왔습: You have been offered a step in rank if you will go to the army in Spain (or the colonies). It is notorious for guerrilla war and fevers.
