You left for the distant garrison. Promotion was quick, but you lost many comrades.
You stayed with the regiment you know.
다른 학자가 당신이 먼저 찾아낸 결과를 자기 이름으로 아카데미에 발표했습: Another scholar has presented to the Academy, under his own name, a result you found first.
날짜가 적힌 연구 노트를 들고 학회에서 반박했습니다. 학계가 둘로 갈렸습: You rebutted him at a meeting, holding your dated notebooks. The learned world split in two.
조용히 다음 연구로 넘어간다: Move quietly on to your next work
You decided to spend the time on the next problem rather than on fighting.
부유한 상인 부부가 초상화를 주문합니다. 몇 달은 큰 역사화를 그릴 시간: A wealthy merchant and his wife commission a portrait. For a few months there will be no time for the great history painting.
The couple were pleased with the picture and introduced you to their friends.
You stood before the great canvas with empty pockets.
경쟁 상인이 손을 잡자고 합니다. 자본은 두 배가 되지만 결정은 함께 해: A rival merchant proposes joining forces. Your capital would double, but decisions would be made together.
You merged the two shops. Your connections grew.
You run the shop your own way.
흉년에 십일조와 미사 헌금을 낼 수 없다는 교구민이 늘었습니다. 주교좌에: In a bad year more and more parishioners say they cannot pay the tithe or the Mass offering. The bishop's office presses you to make up the income.
The parishioners began calling you ‘our priest’.
You won the bishop's confidence, but the church is a little emptier.
The convent has decided to send nursing sisters to the town hospital, where an epidemic is raging.
You went between the beds, caring for the sick.
You took on the children's lessons.
파리에서 새 방법(우두 접종, 나중에는 라에네크의 청진기)이 소개되었습니: A new method has been introduced in Paris (cowpox vaccination; later, Laennec's stethoscope). Your colleagues do not trust it yet.
Patients were suspicious at first, but the results spoke for themselves.
익숙한 방법을 지킨다: Keep to the methods you know
직공들이 임금을 올려 달라며 일손을 놓았습니다. 노동자의 단합은 법으로: The workers have downed tools, demanding higher pay. Combinations of workers are forbidden by law.
You raised wages a little and work started again.
The ringleaders were taken away. The works is running again, but the mood is icy.
Someone holds out an envelope, asking you to hurry through their papers of exemption from conscription.
The envelope was thick. That night you slept badly.
You dealt with the papers in their turn.
Your superior began to take notice of you.
The parish priest wants more catechism lessons and reading taught only from the prayer book.
아이들은 신문과 지도로 읽기를 배웁니다. 신부는 강론에서 당신을 언급했습: The children learn to read from newspapers and maps. The priest mentioned you in his sermon.
검열에 걸린 대본: A script stopped by the censor
A few lines of the new play have been stopped by the censor. The theatre manager wants to change them.
The play went on without trouble.
The audience gave a standing ovation, and the next day the play was banned.
A writer out of favour with the government wants to come to your salon.
그날 밤 대화는 어느 때보다 뜨거웠습니다. 이튿날 경찰 정보원이 집 앞을: That night the conversation was hotter than ever. The next day a police informer was loitering outside the house.
Your new book is almost finished. Some passages are politically sensitive.
The book caused a stir, and your name became known with it.
The book sold, but nobody knows you wrote it.
아기가 거꾸로 서 있습니다. 외과의를 부르면 산모 집안이 큰돈을 내야 합: The baby is breech. If a surgeon is called, the mother's family will have to pay a great deal.
You put your hand in as you were taught and turned the baby. The first cry rang out.
The surgeon came, and mother and child both lived.
A noble customer has not paid for a dress for a year.
You got the money, but that family's friends stopped coming.
The customer apologised and brought other customers.
On a long voyage the food has gone bad, and the sailors vent their anger on the captain.
There was no mutiny. The captain came to trust you.
선원들의 요구를 전한다: Put the sailors' demands to him
The captain increased the rations. The sailors follow you.
Pressure has come to bend the route so that it crosses land owned by a friend of the minister.
The line was bent. News of your promotion came quickly.
기술적으로 맞는 노선을 고집한다: Insist on the technically correct route
Your report was praised, but the minister's side turned cold.
선술집마다 정보원을 두면 사건을 빨리 해결할 수 있습니다. 대신 이웃들이: With an informer in every tavern, cases would be solved quickly. But neighbours would come to suspect one another.
Cases were solved faster, and you won the confidence of those above you.
It is slow, but people in the neighbourhood come to you first.
집세를 빌려 달라는 친구: A friend asks to borrow the rent
어릴 적부터 알던 친구가 서기 자리를 잃고 찾아왔습니다. 이번 분기 집세: A friend you have known since childhood has lost a clerk's post and come to you. If they cannot pay this quarter's rent, the family will be out in the street, so they ask to borrow three months' worth. There is no telling when it would be paid back.
돈은 줄지만 사람이 남는다: Less money, but a friend kept
You handed over the purse. Your friend held your hand for a long time without a word.
형편이 안 된다고 했습니다. 친구는 고개를 끄덕이고 돌아갔지만, 문을 나: You said you could not afford it. Your friend nodded and left, but their face was set as they went out of the door.
이웃의 젊은 서기가 밤늦게 문을 두드렸습니다. 왕비를 조롱하는 금서 꾸러: A young clerk from next door knocked late at night with a bundle of forbidden books mocking the queen. The police are searching the print shops, so he asks you to keep them for a few days. There is a reward for informing.
사흘 뒤 그가 꾸러미를 가져갔습니다. “이 은혜는 잊지 않겠소.”: Three days later he came for the bundle. “I will not forget this kindness.”
다락을 뒤진 경찰에게 벌금을 물었습니다. 그는 끝까지 당신 이름을 대지: The police searched the attic and you were fined. He never gave your name.
You collected the reward. They say he spent months in prison.
모른 척 문을 닫는다: Shut the door and pretend not to know
You acted as if you had seen nothing.
작업장 돈궤에서 돈이 빈 것을 알았습니다. 열여섯 살 도제가 울면서 털어: You found money missing from the workshop cash box. The sixteen-year-old apprentice confessed in tears: it was for medicine for a sick mother.
용서하고 일을 계속 시킨다: Forgive him and keep him on
From then on the boy came in earlier and worked later than anyone.
You packed his things and sent him off. In his livret you wrote ‘thief’.
흉년입니다. 당신 곳간에는 곡식이 넉넉합니다. 밀가루 값은 날마다 오르고: It is a bad year. Your granary is well stocked. The price of flour rises every day, and hungry neighbours ask for credit. If you wait, the price will go higher still.
이웃에게 외상으로 나눈다: Share it with the neighbours on credit
반은 끝내 돌려받지 못했습니다. 그해 겨울 골목에 굶어 죽은 집은 없었습: Half was never paid back. That winter no household in the lane starved.
값이 오를 때까지 기다렸다 판다: Wait for the price to rise and then sell
You sold the grain dear. The neighbours whispered that you were a ‘hoarder’.
새벽에 영주의 숲에서 토끼를 메고 나오는 이웃을 보았습니다. 영주의 사냥: At dawn you saw a neighbour coming out of the lord's woods with a rabbit over his shoulder. The lord's gamekeeper is looking for poachers and promises a reward for information. If caught, it means the galleys.
입을 다물었습니다. 며칠 뒤 이웃이 토끼 다리 하나를 문간에 놓고 갔습니: You kept your mouth shut. A few days later the neighbour left a rabbit's leg on your doorstep.
You took the reward. The neighbour sold his cow to pay the fine.
어느 후작이 당신 솜씨(혹은 장사 수완)를 마음에 들어 합니다. 정기적으: A marquis has taken a liking to your skill (or your head for business). He offers regular orders and his backing in family matters, and has given you the run of his house.
The orders never stopped. Letters stamped with the marquis's arms piled up in your drawer.
You did not want to stand under another man's coat of arms.
헛간에서 군복을 벗어 던진 젊은 병사를 발견했습니다. 맞아 죽을 것 같아: In the barn you found a young soldier who had thrown off his uniform. He says he ran because he thought they would beat him to death. Hiding a deserter is punishable.
숨겨 주고 먹을 것을 준다: Hide him and give him food
사흘 뒤 그는 당신이 준 헌 옷을 입고 떠났습니다. 이름을 묻자 웃기만: Three days later he left wearing the old clothes you gave him. When you asked his name, he only smiled.
본당의 젊은 보좌신부는 주임 신부가 십일조를 다 가져가는 바람에 끼니도: They say the parish's young curate goes without meals because the parish priest takes the whole tithe. You heard he has no firewood for the winter.
신부는 부끄러워하며 받았습니다. “하느님이 갚으실 겁니다.”: The curate accepted, embarrassed. “God will repay you.”
남의 일이라 생각한다: Consider it none of your business
은잔을 깨뜨린 하녀: A maid who broke a silver cup
하녀가 손님용 은잔을 떨어뜨려 찌그러뜨렸습니다. 품삯 몇 년 치 값입니다: The maid dropped one of the silver cups kept for guests and dented it. It is worth several years of her wages. The elders of the household say throw her out at once and hand her to the police.
품삯에서 조금씩 갚게 하고 용서한다: Forgive her and have her pay it back little by little from her wages
하녀는 몇 년을 더 일했습니다. 떠나는 날 당신 아이들을 안고 울었습니다: The maid worked several more years. On the day she left she hugged your children and wept.
You sent her away without a reference. They say she never found a place in another house.
집주인(혹은 영주의 관리)과 가난한 소작인 사이의 송사에 증인으로 불려: You have been called as a witness in a suit between a landlord (or the lord's agent) and a poor tenant. You know the tenant is in the right. But the landlord has power over you too.
The tenant won. The landlord was cold to you ever after.
소작인은 땅을 잃었습니다. 법정을 나서며 그가 당신을 오래 쳐다보았습니다: The tenant lost his land. Leaving the court, he gave you a long look.
황제의 옛 장교가 반급으로 쫓겨나 경찰의 감시를 받고 있습니다. 보나파르: One of the Emperor's old officers, put on half pay, is under police watch. He asks to rent a room for meetings of Bonapartists.
몇 달 동안 밤마다 낮은 목소리가 들렸습니다. 경찰은 끝내 오지 않았습니: For months you heard low voices every night. The police never came.
He was arrested, and you received a letter of thanks from the police commissioner.
징집을 피한 이웃 아들: A neighbour's son dodging the draft
The neighbours' son drew a bad number in the conscription lottery and fled to the woods. The gendarmes are searching the village and say any house that hides him will be fined. Tonight he knocks at your barn door.
헌병은 헛간을 그냥 지나쳤습니다. 이듬해 그는 대리인을 사서 돌아왔고,: The gendarmes walked straight past the barn. The following year he bought a substitute, came back, and settled in the village.
헌병이 짚더미에서 그를 끌어냈고, 당신은 벌금을 물었습니다. 그래도 그는: The gendarmes dragged him out of the straw and you paid a fine. Still, he never forgot that night.
그는 끌려가 연대로 보내졌습니다. 몇 해 뒤 다리 하나를 절며 돌아왔습니: He was taken and sent to a regiment. Years later he came back limping on one leg.
이웃집 아들이 징집 제비뽑기에서 나쁜 번호를 뽑고 달아났습니다. 경찰이: The neighbours' son drew a bad number in the conscription lottery and ran. The police are searching the lanes and say any house that hides him will be fined. Tonight he knocks at the door of your attic room.
이웃집 아들이 징집 제비뽑기에서 나쁜 번호를 뽑고 달아났습니다. 헌병이: The neighbours' son drew a bad number in the conscription lottery and ran. The gendarmes are searching the lanes of {고향} and say any house that hides him will be fined. Tonight he knocks at the back door of your workshop.
파리의 집세가 또 올랐습니다. 식구들은 좁은 셋방에서 기침을 하고, 일감: The rent in Paris has gone up again. The family coughs in a cramped rented room, and work comes and goes. Moving out to a faubourg beyond the walls would halve the rent, and country relatives in your parents' home region say come down and farm with them.
성벽 밖 포부르로 옮긴다: Move to a faubourg beyond the walls
집세를 아낌 / 먼 출퇴근: Saving on rent / a long way to work
생앙투안 포부르 끝의 셋방으로 옮겼습니다. 같은 돈으로 방이 하나 더 생: You moved to rooms at the far end of the Faubourg Saint-Antoine. For the same money you have one more room.
You leave at five in the morning and come back at night. You hardly see the children.
가족을 데리고 시골 친척에게 내려간다: Take the family down to the country relatives
땅과 공기 / 낯선 시골: Land and air / a strange countryside
친척의 밭 한쪽을 빌려 감자와 밀을 심었습니다. 아이들의 뺨에 다시 혈색: You rented a corner of a relative's field and planted potatoes and wheat. The colour came back to the children's cheeks.
‘파리 사람’이라는 꼬리표가 몇 해 동안 붙어 다녔습니다. 농사일도 손에: For years the label ‘the Parisian’ followed you. Farm work never came easily to your hands.
You did not think you could live anywhere but Paris.
글을 깨침 / 더딤 / 포기: Learning to read / slow / giving up
글자는 알아보지만 읽는 데 한참 걸립니다. 서명은 할 수 있게 되었지만,: You can make out the letters, but reading takes a long time. You can sign your name now, but a page of a book is still hard going.
The work was hard and you nodded off every evening. You stopped after a few weeks.
이 나이에 무슨 글이냐며 사양한다: Decline: what use are letters at your age?
You have lived without letters until now.
배우자는 글을 압니다. 저녁마다 한 줄씩 가르쳐 주겠다고 합니다. 부끄럽: Your spouse can read. They offer to teach you a line every evening. It is embarrassing, but you are tired of asking others to read your letters.
배우자에게서 몇 달 만에 기도서와 신문을 더듬더듬 읽게 되었습니다. 처음: In a few months your spouse had you stumbling through the prayer book and the newspaper. For the first time you signed your own name.
하사가 되려면 글을 알아야 합니다. 연대에 저녁 학교가 있고, 글을 아는: To be made corporal you must be able to read. The regiment has an evening school, and a comrade who can read offers to teach you.
연대 학교 몇 달 만에 기도서와 신문을 더듬더듬 읽게 되었습니다. 처음으: After a few months of the regimental school you could stumble through the prayer book and the newspaper. For the first time you signed your own name.
콜레주(리세)를 마쳤습니다. 아버지는 집안에 어울리는 길을 고르라고 합니: You have finished the collège (lycée). Your father tells you to choose a road befitting the family. The faculty of law makes advocates, the faculty of medicine makes doctors. There is the seminary, the military schools and, after 1794, the École polytechnique. Or you could take over the family business straight away.
법학부에 간다: Go to the faculty of law
로마법과 관습법, 법원의 변론을 배웠습니다. 학위를 받고 변호사 명부에: You learned Roman law and customary law and how to plead in court. You took your degree and were entered on the roll of advocates.
의학부(의학교)에 간다: Go to the faculty (school) of medicine
해부실과 병원 회진의 몇 해였습니다. 학위 논문을 내고 의사가 되었습니다: Years of the dissecting room and hospital rounds. You submitted your thesis and became a doctor.
You put on the black cassock of the seminary of Saint-Sulpice.
You finished military school and were commissioned as a sub-lieutenant.
몽주가 세운 이공대학의 제복을 입었습니다. 졸업하고 토목 기사가 되었습니: You put on the uniform of the École polytechnique founded by Monge. You graduated and became a civil engineer.
Your hands shook in front of the mathematics examiner. The following year you went to the faculty of law.
문학부(고등사범)에 가서 교수가 된다: Go to the faculty of letters (the École normale) and become a teacher
By way of the École normale you took your place at the front of a lycée classroom.
학교를 마치고 집안 일을 잇는다: Finish school and take over the family business
You learned your father's firm (or the estate) and took over the books.
선거인 집회가 열립니다. 클럽과 구역에서 이름이 알려진 당신을 의원 후보: The electoral assembly is meeting. Since your name is known in the clubs and the section, there is talk of putting you forward as a candidate. Each département sends a dozen or so deputies, and there are dozens of candidates. Whether to the Legislative Assembly (1791) or the Convention (1792), those elected will decide the fate of France in the hall in Paris.
선거인 집회에서 세 번의 투표 끝에 이름이 불렸습니다. 국민 대표 의원으: After three ballots in the electoral assembly, your name was called. You go to Paris as a deputy of the nation.
선거인 수백 명 가운데 당신 이름을 아는 사람은 몇 되지 않았습니다. 첫: Among hundreds of electors, few knew your name. You fell at the first ballot and went back to the business of the section.
지금 의원이 된다는 것이 무엇을 뜻하는지 알기에, 이름을 거두어 달라고: Knowing what it means to become a deputy now, you asked them to withdraw your name.
국민공회의 의사당은 계단식입니다. 왼쪽 높은 자리의 ‘산’에는 로베스피에: The Convention's hall rises in tiers. On the high benches to the left, the ‘Mountain’, sit Robespierre, Danton and Marat; on the right, the Girondins of Brissot and Vergniaud; and in the low seats in the middle, the quiet majority called the ‘Plain’. Where you sit is your fate.
The Jacobin Club and the sections of Paris are on your side.
You stand with the provinces, with law and order. The people of Paris hate you.
At every vote you watch which way the wind blows. These are the seats of those who survive.
카페와 살롱에서 볼테르와 루소의 이야기가 오갑니다. 왕의 권위는 하늘이: In cafés and salons people talk of Voltaire and Rousseau. Some say the king's authority comes from heaven; others say taxes and privileges must be reformed. Which way does your heart lean?
왕과 교회의 질서를 믿는다: Trust the order of king and Church
전하께서 백성을 굽어살피신다고 믿습니다. 개혁가들의 떠들썩함이 못마땅합니: You believe His Majesty watches over his people. The reformers' clamour displeases you.
세금과 특권을 고쳐야 한다고 생각한다: Think taxes and privileges must be reformed
You passed round pamphlets saying a parliament should check the king, as in England.
신분제 자체가 잘못되었다고 생각한다: Think the system of estates itself is wrong
루소의 『사회 계약론』 한 구절을 외우고 다닙니다. “인간은 자유롭게 태: You go about reciting a line of Rousseau's Social Contract: “Man is born free, and everywhere he is in chains.”
누가 위에 앉든 빵값과 세금이 문제입니다. 정치 이야기가 나오면 자리를: Whoever sits on top, what matters is the price of bread and the taxes. When talk turned to politics, you left the room.
혁명 속에서 어디에 서는가: Where you stand in the Revolution
구역 회의와 클럽, 신문과 팸플릿이 저마다 편을 가르라고 합니다. 입헌: The section assemblies and clubs, the newspapers and pamphlets all demand that you take sides. Some want to keep the constitutional monarchy, some to found a republic, some to return to the old monarchy.
왕과 옛 질서를 지지한다: Support the king and the old order
삼색 휘장 대신 주머니 속에 흰 휘장을 넣고 다닙니다. 입 밖에 내기는: Instead of the tricolour cockade, you carry a white one in your pocket. It is a dangerous thought to speak aloud.
헌법과 왕이 함께 가야 한다고 믿습니다. 라파예트의 국민방위대가 믿음직합: You believe the constitution and the king must go together. Lafayette's National Guard seems reliable.
브리소와 롤랑 부인의 신문을 읽습니다. 공화국은 좋지만 파리 민중의 폭력: You read the papers of Brissot and Madame Roland. A republic is fine, but the violence of the Paris crowd frightens you.
“The fatherland is in danger!” Your heart races at the speeches in the Jacobin Club.
제1통령이 황제가 되었습니다. 질서와 영광을 가져왔다는 사람도, 공화국을: The First Consul has become Emperor. Some say he brought order and glory, some that he stole the Republic, some that the rightful royal house must return.
아우스터리츠의 승전보에 모자를 던졌습니다. 혁명의 성과를 지키는 것은 황: At the news of Austerlitz you threw your hat in the air. It is the Emperor who safeguards what the Revolution won.
정통 왕가의 귀환을 바란다: Hope for the return of the rightful royal house
You pray in secret for Louis XVIII in exile.
On the day the republican calendar was abolished, you emptied your glass without a word.
부르봉 왕가가 돌아왔습니다. 혁명 이전으로 되돌리자는 극왕당파, 헌장을: The Bourbons are back. There are the Ultras, who would turn the clock back to before the Revolution; the liberals, who would uphold the Charter; the Bonapartists, who miss the Emperor; and the republicans, holding their breath.
「라 코티디엔」을 구독합니다. 혁명이 남긴 것은 모두 지워야 한다고 믿습: You subscribe to La Quotidienne. You believe everything the Revolution left behind must be wiped away.
「르 콩스티튀시오넬」을 읽고, 선거 때마다 자유주의 후보에게 마음이 갑니: You read Le Constitutionnel, and at every election your heart goes to the liberal candidate.
You keep a small bust of the Emperor hidden somewhere in the house.
비밀 결사의 공화파 (카르보나리): A republican of the secret societies (the Carbonari)
By lamplight you swore the Carbonari oath.
외동에게 남길 것: What to leave an only child
공증인을 불러 유언장을 쓸 때가 되었습니다. 자식은 하나뿐이니 나눌 다툼: It is time to call the notary and make your will. With only one child, there will be no quarrel over shares. What troubles you is the old age of the one left behind, and whether your child's in-laws will lay hands on the property.
모두 외동에게 물려준다: Leave everything to your only child
The will took a single page. Your child took your hand without a word.
배우자에게 평생 사용권(용익권)을 남기고, 소유는 자식에게: Leave your spouse the use of it for life (usufruct), and the ownership to your child
공증인이 “용익권”이라는 낯선 말을 설명했습니다. 배우자는 죽을 때까지: The notary explained the strange word “usufruct”. Your spouse will live in this house until death, and then it passes to your child.
재산의 십분의 일을 구빈원과 교구 학교에 남겼습니다. 자식은 조금 서운한: You left a tenth of your estate to the hospice and the parish school. Your child seemed a little hurt.
It is time to call the notary and make your will. You have no child to inherit. Left as it is, the law will divide it in its set order among your brothers and sisters, nephews and nieces.
조카들에게 나눠 준다: Divide it among your nephews and nieces
조카들이 공증인 사무실에 모였습니다. 얼굴을 처음 보는 조카도 있었습니다: Your nephews and nieces gathered at the notary's office. Some of them you had never seen before.
평생 곁에 있어 준 사람에게 남긴다: Leave it to the one who stayed by your side all your life
오래 돌봐 준 이웃(하녀)에게 집과 살림을 남겼습니다. 친척들이 소송을: You left the house and its contents to the neighbour (or maid) who cared for you for so long. The relatives muttered about going to law.
구빈원과 교구 학교에 기부한다: Give it to the hospice and the parish school
유언장에 따라 구빈원에 침대 둘이 생기고, 교구 학교에 당신 이름의 장학: Under your will, two beds were endowed at the hospice and a scholarship in your name at the parish school.
종신 연금으로 바꿔 남은 생을 편하게 산다: Turn it into a life annuity and live the rest of your days in comfort
집을 종신 연금(비아제)으로 팔았습니다. 매달 연금이 들어옵니다. 산 사: You sold the house en viager, for a life annuity. Each month the annuity comes in. The buyer will be hoping you do not live long.
제1통령의 시대: The age of the First Consul
브뤼메르의 쿠데타로 보나파르트 장군이 제1통령이 되었습니다. 혁명을 끝내: The coup of Brumaire has made General Bonaparte First Consul. Some say he has ended the Revolution and restored order, some that the Republic has been handed to a soldier, some that he will bring back the king.
이탈리아에서 승전보가 들려오고 거리의 소란이 잦아들었습니다. 십 년 만에: Victories are reported from Italy and the turmoil in the streets has died down. For the first time in ten years, you feel the country is working.
보나파르트가 몽크 장군처럼 왕을 다시 모셔 오리라 기대했지만, 그럴 사람: You hoped Bonaparte would bring back the king as General Monck once did, but it grows ever clearer he is not that kind of man.
헌법을 몇 번이나 고친 끝에 결국 장군 한 사람이 권력을 쥐었을 뿐이라고: After so many constitutions, you think, all that has happened is that one general has taken power.
보나파르트가 세운 특별 군사학교(처음엔 퐁텐블로, 1808년부터 생시르): The special military school founded by Bonaparte (first at Fontainebleau, at Saint-Cyr from 1808) is taking cadets. There are fees to pay, but graduates are commissioned as sub-lieutenants straight away.
황제가 돌아왔다: 연대의 선택: The Emperor is back: the regiment's choice
엘바섬을 떠난 황제가 그르노블로 다가옵니다. 국왕의 명령은 “찬탈자를 막: The Emperor has left Elba and is nearing Grenoble. The king's order is “Stop the usurper.” But the soldiers are already pulling the old tricolour cockades out of their packs.
연대와 함께 황제 편으로 넘어간다: Go over to the Emperor with the regiment
“황제 만세!” 연대 전체가 독수리 깃발 아래로 넘어갔습니다. 석 달 뒤: “Vive l'Empereur!” The whole regiment went over to the eagle. Three months later, Waterloo awaits.
루이 18세를 따라 벨기에 헨트로 떠났습니다. 워털루 뒤 왕과 함께 돌아: You followed Louis XVIII to Ghent in Belgium and came back with the king after Waterloo. The king did not forget the loyal.
명령도 충성도 흐려진 석 달이었습니다. 왕이 돌아오자 ‘기회주의자’라는: Three months in which orders and loyalty alike grew blurred. When the king returned, you were labelled a ‘turncoat’.
샹 드 마르스의 연대: The regiment on the Champ de Mars
7월, 왕은 파리 주변에 2만 명의 군대를 모았습니다. 당신의 연대도 샹: In July the king gathered twenty thousand troops around Paris. Your regiment too has pitched camp on the Champ de Mars. The French Guards, they say, have already gone over to the crowd. On the morning of the 14th, shots ring out from the direction of the Bastille.
프랑스 근위대 동료들과 대포를 끌고 바스티유로 간다: Haul the cannon to the Bastille with your comrades of the French Guards
위랭 하사와 엘리 중위를 따라 대포 다섯 문을 요새 앞에 세웠습니다. 그: Following Sergeant Hulin and Lieutenant Élie, you set five cannon before the fortress. By evening you were a ‘conqueror of the Bastille’.
You were hit by a shot fired from the walls.
명령은 끝내 오지 않았습니다. 베장발 남작은 군대를 물렸고, 왕은 파리로: The order never came. Baron de Besenval withdrew the troops, and the king came to Paris and accepted the tricolour cockade.
(귀족 장교) 병사들이 이탈하지 못하게 다잡는다: (Noble officer) Keep the men from deserting
병사들의 눈빛이 이미 달라져 있었습니다. 그날 밤 부대의 절반이 사라졌습: The look in the soldiers' eyes had already changed. That night half the unit vanished. An age has come when a noble officer's orders no longer carry.
오늘 라 뮈에트 성 정원에서 몽골피에 형제의 열기구가 사람을 태우고 떠오: Today, they say, the Montgolfier brothers' balloon will rise from the gardens of the Château de la Muette carrying men. All Paris is flocking to watch.

일 때문에 가지 못했습니다. 저녁에 이웃들이 하늘을 나는 사람 이야기로: Work kept you from going. In the evening the neighbours could talk of nothing but the man who flew.
7월 14일 아침. 앵발리드에서 총을 손에 넣은 군중이 화약을 찾아 생앙: The morning of 14 July. Having seized muskets at the Invalides, the crowd surges towards the fortress of the Bastille by the Porte Saint-Antoine in search of powder. The tocsin rings in every street.
군중과 함께 요새로 간다: Go to the fortress with the crowd
함락의 현장 / 부상 / 전사: There when it falls / wounded / killed
오후 다섯 시, 도개교가 내려왔습니다. 당신은 함성 속에서 요새 안마당에: At five in the afternoon the drawbridge came down. Amid the roar you stepped into the inner courtyard. One day your name will be on the list of the ‘conquerors of the Bastille’.
총탄에 다쳤습니다: You were hit by a musket ball
요새 위에서 쏜 총알이 팔을 스쳤습니다. 피를 흘리며 끌려 나왔지만, 저: A shot from the walls grazed your arm. You were carried out bleeding, but in the evening you heard the fortress had fallen.
안마당 앞에서 쓰러졌습니다. 이날 공격자 가운데 약 백 명이 목숨을 잃었: You fell before the inner courtyard. About a hundred of the attackers lost their lives that day.
바리케이드용 돌과 음식을 나른다: Carry paving stones for barricades, and food
Hearing the gunfire in the distance, you carried bread and water to people.
문을 걸어 잠그고 집에 머물렀습니다. 바깥의 함성은 밤늦게까지 이어졌습니: You bolted the door and stayed at home. The roar outside went on late into the night.
10월 5일, 빵을 구하지 못한 시장 아낙들이 시청 앞에 모여 베르사유로: On 5 October the market women, unable to find bread, gather outside the Hôtel de Ville and cry out to march to Versailles. Rain is falling, yet the procession swells to thousands.
국왕 일가를 파리로 / 혼란 속 부상: The royal family to Paris / hurt in the turmoil
“빵집 주인과 안주인, 꼬마 견습생”을 데려왔습니다: You brought back “the baker, the baker's wife and the baker's boy”
밤새 궁 앞에서 버텼습니다. 이튿날 국왕 일가가 파리로 옮겨 가는 마차: You held out all night before the palace. The next day you walked back behind the carriages bringing the royal family to Paris.
궁 안의 소동 속에 다쳤습니다: You were hurt in the tumult inside the palace
At dawn you fell and were hurt in the crowd that burst into the palace.
You watched the procession go by from the window.
(군인) 국민방위대로 행렬을 따라 베르사유로 간다: (Soldier) Follow the march to Versailles with the National Guard
라파예트를 따라 밤길을 걸었습니다. 새벽에 궁으로 몰려든 군중과 근위대: You marched through the night behind Lafayette. At dawn you stood between the crowd storming the palace and the Life Guards.
바스티유 함락 1주년, 파리 샹 드 마르스에서 전국의 국민방위대 대표가: On the first anniversary of the fall of the Bastille, delegates of the National Guards of the whole country gather on the Champ de Mars to swear loyalty to the nation, the law and the king. Every village holds a festival the same day.
축제에 참여해 맹세한다: Join the festival and take the oath
제단 앞에서 사람들과 함께 손을 들어 맹세했습니다. 신분이 다른 사람들이: Before the altar you raised your hand and swore with the others. People of different estates sat at one table.
You heard the drums and the cheering from afar.
(군인) 연대 대표로 조국의 제단 앞에 선다: (Soldier) Stand before the altar of the fatherland for your regiment
연대의 깃발을 들고 샹 드 마르스의 제단 앞에서 맹세했습니다. 장교와 사: You carried the regiment's colours and took the oath before the altar on the Champ de Mars. Officers and men stood in one line.
(귀족) 칭호를 내려놓고 시민으로 맹세한다: (Noble) Lay down your title and swear as a citizen
두 달 전 세습 귀족 칭호가 폐지되었습니다. 문장 없는 외투를 입고 시민: Two months ago hereditary titles were abolished. Wearing a coat without arms, you took the oath among the citizens.
탈레랑 주교가 집전하는 제단 미사에 사제들이 줄지어 섰습니다. 비가 쏟아: Priests stood in rows at the altar Mass said by Bishop Talleyrand. The rain poured down, but three hundred thousand people knelt.
샹 드 마르스의 청원: The petition of the Champ de Mars
국왕이 도주하다 붙잡힌 뒤, 코르들리에 클럽이 국왕 폐위 청원서에 서명하: After the king was caught fleeing, the Cordeliers Club calls people to the Champ de Mars to sign a petition for his deposition. There are rumours that martial law has been declared.
조국의 제단 위 청원서에 이름을 적었습니다. 저녁 무렵 그곳에서 총성이: You wrote your name on the petition laid on the altar of the fatherland. Towards evening, hearing that shots had rung out there, you shuddered.
The red flag went up and shots rang out. You fell in the crowd and were hurt.
총탄을 피하지 못했습니다: You could not escape the bullets
Dozens lost their lives on the Champ de Mars that day.
(군인·국민방위대) 광장 경비에 선다: (Soldier · National Guard) Stand guard on the square
발포 명령이 떨어졌습니다: The order to fire was given
계엄령의 붉은 깃발이 오르고, 총구가 군중을 향했습니다. 당신도 방아쇠를: The red flag of martial law went up and the muskets turned on the crowd. You pulled the trigger too. That night you could not sleep.
You raised your musket to the sky. You hoped no one had seen.
의회가 “조국이 위험에 처했다”고 선언했습니다. 광장에 천막이 세워지고: The Assembly has declared “the fatherland in danger”. Tents have gone up in the squares and the registers of volunteers lie open.
명부에 이름을 적고 삼색 휘장을 받았습니다. 며칠 뒤 대대와 함께 동부: You wrote your name in the register and were given a tricolour cockade. In a few days you leave with the battalion for the eastern front.
You saw your departing friends off.
경종이 밤새 울렸습니다. 구역의 상퀼로트와 마르세유 연맹병이 튈르리 궁으: The tocsin rang all night. The sans-culottes of the sections and the fédérés of Marseille are advancing on the Tuileries palace. The palace is held by the Swiss Guards.
왕정의 몰락 / 부상 / 전사: The fall of the monarchy / wounded / killed
궁이 함락되고 국왕 일가는 의회로 피신했습니다. 왕정의 마지막 날을 눈앞: The palace was taken and the royal family took refuge with the Assembly. You saw the last day of the monarchy with your own eyes.
계단에서 총상을 입었습니다: You were shot on the staircase
You went down under the Guards' volley and were carried out by your comrades.
궁 앞마당에서 쓰러졌습니다: You fell in the palace forecourt
Hundreds of the attackers were killed or wounded that day.
9월 20일, 발미 언덕. 프로이센군이 안개 속에서 다가옵니다. 켈레르만: 20 September, the heights of Valmy. The Prussians advance out of the fog. General Kellermann puts his hat on the point of his sword and cries “Vive la Nation!”
대열을 지키며 함께 외친다: Hold the line and cry out with him
포격전 끝에 적이 물러났습니다. 이튿날 공화국이 선포되었다는 소식이 전해: After the cannonade the enemy withdrew. The next day word came that the Republic had been proclaimed.
포탄 파편에 맞았습니다: You were hit by a shell splinter
You spent several weeks in the field hospital.
두려움에 대열 뒤로 물러난다: Shrink back behind the line in fear
You were ashamed, but you survived.
혁명 광장의 아침: Morning on the Place de la Révolution
1월 21일. 시민 루이 카페가 혁명 광장의 단두대에 오릅니다. 새벽부터: 21 January. Citizen Louis Capet mounts the scaffold in the Place de la Révolution. The drums have been beating since dawn, and troops line the streets.
군중 사이로 북소리가 그치는 순간을 보았습니다. 누군가는 환호했고, 누군: Among the crowd you saw the moment the drums fell silent. Some cheered; some turned their heads away.
You closed the shutters and prayed. The church bells did not ring.
You went to work. The streets were strangely quiet.
북소리가 왕의 마지막 말을 덮었습니다. 당신은 처형대를 등지고 서 있었습: The drums drowned out the king's last words. You stood with your back to the scaffold.
(왕당파) 몰래 상복을 입고 미사를 올린다: (Royalist) Put on mourning in secret and hear Mass
In a cellar, a non-juring priest said Mass for the king.
A neighbour told the watch committee. A few days later you were arrested and taken to prison.
30만 명 징집령과 서부의 봉기: The levy of 300,000 and the rising in the west
At the news that the Republic is conscripting three hundred thousand men, the villages of the west have risen. In the woods the ‘Chouans’, who use the hoot of an owl as their signal, are gathering men.
숲속의 전쟁 / 체포 / 전사: War in the woods / captured / killed
숲에서 몇 해를 버텼습니다: You held out in the woods for years
낮에는 밭을 갈고 밤에는 숲에서 공화국군 호송대를 습격했습니다. 마을 사: By day you ploughed, by night you ambushed republican convoys in the woods. The villagers secretly brought you food.
공화국군에게 붙잡혔습니다: You were taken by the republican army
You spent months in prison and were freed under an amnesty.
숲에서 돌아오지 못했습니다: You did not come back from the woods
You joined the republican army. The people of your home region turned their backs on you.
아무 편도 들지 않고 숨어 지낸다: Take no side and lie low
You lived holding your breath, keeping out of sight of both sides.
리옹이 국민공회에 맞서 봉기하자 공화국군이 도시를 포위했습니다. 포탄이: Lyon rose against the Convention, and the republican army has laid siege to the city. Shells are falling and bread is running out.
버팀 / 함락 후 처벌 / 전사: Holding out / punished after the fall / killed
두 달을 버텼습니다: You held out for two months
10월에 도시가 함락되었습니다. 당신은 이름이 명부에 오르지 않아 살아남: The city fell in October. Your name was not on the lists, and you survived.
함락 뒤 투옥되었습니다: You were imprisoned after the fall
혁명 재판소에 끌려갔다가 겨우 풀려났습니다. 많은 이웃이 브로토 평원에서: You were taken before the revolutionary tribunal and barely released. Many of your neighbours were shot on the Brotteaux plain.
You fell below the hill of Fourvière.
밤에 론강을 건너 친척 집으로 피신했습니다. 집과 작업장은 남겨 두었습니: At night you crossed the Rhône and took refuge with relatives. You left house and workshop behind.
You hid in the cellar and endured the bombardment.
최고 존재의 제전: The Festival of the Supreme Being

화가 다비드가 꾸민 거대한 무대를 보았습니다. 사람들은 즐거워했지만, 뒤: You saw the vast stage designed by the painter David. People enjoyed it, but you heard muttering behind it too.
You kept to the back streets to avoid the procession.
국민공회가 로베스피에르를 체포했습니다. 파리 코뮌은 그를 구하자고 구역들: The Convention has arrested Robespierre. The Paris Commune is ringing the tocsin in the sections to rescue him. You must decide which side to stand on.
시청 앞 코뮌 편으로 간다: Go to the Hôtel de Ville, on the Commune's side
비가 내리고 사람들이 흩어졌습니다: Rain fell and the crowd scattered
자정이 넘자 광장의 사람들이 하나둘 돌아갔습니다. 당신도 집으로 돌아왔습: After midnight the people in the square drifted home one by one. You went home too.
체포 명단에 올랐습니다: Your name went on the arrest list
You spent several weeks in prison.
You went to the Hôtel de Ville with the Convention's forces. The Terror was over.
From the window you listened to the rain and the tocsin.
(군인·헌병) 의회 편 부대와 함께 시청에 들어간다: (Soldier · gendarme) Enter the Hôtel de Ville with the Convention's troops
새벽 두 시, 시청 계단을 뛰어올랐습니다. 총성이 울렸고, 로베스피에르가: At two in the morning you ran up the steps of the Hôtel de Ville. A shot rang out, and Robespierre was hit in the jaw.
왕당파에 가까운 구역들이 국민공회에 맞서 무장했습니다. 국민공회는 젊은: Sections close to the royalists have armed themselves against the Convention. The Convention, they say, has put a young artillery officer, Bonaparte, in charge of its defence.
The cannon fired in front of the church of Saint-Roch. You barely got clear.
포도탄을 피하지 못했습니다: You could not escape the grapeshot
You fell on the church steps.
You kept the shop shut until the cannon fell silent.
(왕당파) 왕당파 구역의 봉기에 가담한다: (Royalist) Join the rising of the royalist sections
생로슈 성당 앞에서 젊은 보나파르트 장군의 포도탄이 쏟아졌습니다. 골목으: Before the church of Saint-Roch, young General Bonaparte's grapeshot rained down. You scattered into the alleys.
You fell on the church steps.
사블롱에서 끌어온 대포로 생로슈 성당 앞을 쓸었습니다. 그날 밤 ‘포도탄: With the cannon hauled in from Les Sablons you swept the front of Saint-Roch. That night the nickname ‘General Grapeshot’ was born.
12월 2일, 나폴레옹이 노트르담 대성당에서 황제로 즉위합니다. 몹시 추: On 2 December Napoleon is crowned Emperor in the cathedral of Notre-Dame. It is a bitterly cold day, yet the streets are full of onlookers.
행렬을 보러 나간다: Go out to see the procession
금빛 마차가 지나갈 때 사람들이 “황제 만세!”를 외쳤습니다. 손이 꽁꽁: As the golden coach went by, people cried “Vive l'Empereur!” Your hands were frozen stiff.
장식 일을 맡아 품삯을 번다: Earn wages working on the decorations
You worked putting up triumphal decorations and lamps.
In your warm house you listened to the stories the neighbours brought.
12월 2일 새벽, 프라첸 고지의 안개가 걷히고 해가 떠오릅니다. 대열: At dawn on 2 December the fog lifts from the Pratzen Heights and the sun rises. The order to attack comes down the line.
저녁에 황제가 병사들 앞을 지나갔습니다. “아우스터리츠에 있었다고만 말하: In the evening the Emperor rode past the troops. “You need only say, ‘I was at Austerlitz,’ and people will answer, ‘There goes a brave man!’”
You were carried off the frozen field on a stretcher.
예비대에 남기를 청한다: Ask to stay with the reserve
You heard the guns from the rear.
대육군 60만이 네만강을 건너 러시아로 들어갑니다. 끝없는 평원과 먼지,: The six hundred thousand men of the Grande Armée cross the Niemen into Russia. Endless plains and dust, and for now it is still summer.
본대와 함께 모스크바로 행군한다: March on Moscow with the main army
모스크바가 불타는 것을 보았고, 베레지나강을 건넜습니다. 얼어붙은 발가락: You saw Moscow burn and crossed the Berezina. You came back missing two frozen toes.
러시아군의 포로가 되었습니다: You were taken prisoner by the Russians
You spent two years in a camp near Siberia before coming home.
눈밭에서 돌아오지 못했습니다: You did not come back from the snow
퇴각길의 추위와 굶주림 속에서 쓰러졌습니다. 이 원정에서 수십만 명이 돌: You fell to the cold and hunger of the retreat. Hundreds of thousands never came back from this campaign.
보급 부대 전출을 청한다: Ask to be transferred to the supply train
후방 근무 / 그래도 퇴각길: Duty in the rear / the retreat all the same
폴란드의 보급 기지에 남았습니다: You stayed at the supply depot in Poland
You heard of the horrors at the front only by rumour.
결국 퇴각길에 휩쓸렸습니다: In the end you were swept into the retreat
You barely came back alive through the hunger and cold.
엘바섬을 탈출한 나폴레옹이 군대를 이끌고 북쪽으로 올라오고 있습니다. 보: Napoleon has escaped from Elba and is marching north with an army. Every force sent against him, they say, goes over to the Emperor.
거리로 나가 황제를 맞는다: Go out into the street to greet the Emperor
Amid cries of “Vive l'Empereur!” you pinned the tricolour cockade on again.
You put the white cockade away deep in a drawer. You quietly bide your time.
Once again you watched the world change from your window.
(군인) 연대와 함께 황제 편으로 넘어간다: (Soldier) Go over to the Emperor with the regiment
라프레 들판에서 황제가 외투를 열어 보였습니다. “황제를 쏘고 싶은 병사: On the field of Laffrey the Emperor threw open his greatcoat. “If there is a soldier among you who wants to kill his Emperor, here I am!” No one fired.
(왕당파 장교) 국왕을 따라 헨트로 간다: (Royalist officer) Follow the king to Ghent
루이 18세를 따라 벨기에 헨트로 떠났습니다. 석 달 뒤 워털루가 끝나고: You followed Louis XVIII to Ghent in Belgium. Three months later, when Waterloo was over, you came back with the king. The king did not forget the loyal.
6월 18일, 비에 젖은 벨기에의 들판. 정오에 포격이 시작되고, 저녁에: 18 June, rain-soaked fields in Belgium. The bombardment begins at noon, and in the evening the Guard goes forward in its last charge.
끝까지 대열을 지킨다: Hold the line to the end
When the Prussians appeared the line broke. You walked south all night.
다리에 총상을 입었습니다: You were shot in the leg
You lay on the field a whole day before you were rescued.
Tens of thousands were killed or wounded in that one day.
You heard of the defeat in the rear.
“산적 떼가 곡식을 베러 온다!” 소문이 마을에서 마을로 번집니다. 사람: “Brigands are coming to cut the grain!” The rumour spreads from village to village. People gather with sickles and pitchforks, and someone cries out to go to the lord's château and burn the registers of dues.
무리와 함께 성으로 가 장부를 불태운다: Go to the château with the crowd and burn the registers
장부가 불길 속에 사라졌습니다: The registers went up in flames
